articles.title: Festival of lights turns grim for many as firecracker injuries surge across Bengaluru hospitals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two burn victims, including a seven-month-old pregnant woman and an eight-year-old boy, are critical; they are being treated in the ICU of the Mahabodhi Burns Centre at Victoria Hospital

The festival of lights turned grim for several people in Bengaluru, with over 200 suffering firecracker-related injuries during Deepavali, including many facing the risk of partial or severe vision loss.

Children, including toddlers as young as two and three years old, and elderly people aged up to 70 were among those affected. A significant proportion of the victims were bystanders who were not even bursting crackers.
The dangers were not limited to eye injuries. At the Mahabodhi Burns Centre in the State-run Victoria Hospital, seven patients were admitted with significant firecracker-related burn injuries.

Two of them, a 27-year-old pregnant woman who suffered 33% deep burns, including a blast injury to her leg, and an eight-year-old boy who sustained 20% deep burns after a petrol-filled bottle caught fire and was thrown during a firecracker-related incident, are critical. Both are undergoing treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), while the remaining five patients are stable and receiving treatment in the High Dependency Unit (HDU).
Six other patients with minor firecracker burns were treated as outpatients, said C.N. Yogishwarappa, Professor and Head, Department of Plastic Surgery, at the hospital.

Hospitals across the city have reported a surge in eye injuries. Narayana Nethralaya treated 114 patients across its Bengaluru centres, while the State-run Minto Ophthalmic Hospital reported 50 cases between November 6 and 11. Sankara Eye Hospital recorded 33 patient entries, Nethradhama treated 12, Prabha Eye Clinic reported 15, and Dr. M.C. Modi Charitable Eye Hospital recorded five cases.

At Minto Ophthalmic Hospital, 30 of the 50 patients suffered grievous injuries and were at risk of partial vision loss, while 20 sustained simple injuries, according to hospital director Dr. Suresh Babu.
Bystanders accounted for 30 cases, while children made up 20 of the injured. Eleven patients were admitted, three underwent surgery, and the remaining patients were treated as outpatients.

Dr. Babu said the number of cases could exceed the 56 reported last year as more patients were expected to approach the hospital. He suggested that shops selling firecrackers provide protective glasses free of cost to buyers.

At Narayana Nethralaya, 64 patients were treated at the Rajajinagar branch between November 7 and 10, including 33 children and 23 bystanders. Three patients required surgery, while 61 received medical treatment. Across its other centres at Bommasandra, Bannerghatta Road and Whitefield, a subsequent hospital update reported another 56 patients, including 30 children and 12 bystanders. Three patients suffered severe corneal tears requiring surgery. Two toddlers, aged two and three, sustained injuries after soot particles entered their eyes. The oldest patient, aged 70, suffered a conjunctival laceration.

Rohit Shetty, Director, Narayana Nethralaya Eye Hospitals, said the number of children and innocent bystanders among the injured was particularly concerning. He cautioned that seemingly minor injuries could result in prolonged treatment, permanent visual impairment, and lasting trauma.

Sankara Eye Hospital recorded 33 patient entries, predominantly involving firecracker-related eye injuries. The hospital cautioned against rubbing the eyes or using home remedies and stressed the need for immediate consultation with an ophthalmologist.

articles.title: Collector calls for coordinated efforts among departments to make Kurnool drug-free
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing a meeting, A. Siri directs officials to take strict action against those involved in the illegal trade

The Kurnool district administration has intensified its fight against drug trafficking and consumption, with Collector A. Siri directing officials to take strict action against those involved in the illegal trade.

At a Narcotics Coordination Centre meeting held at the Collectorate on Wednesday, the Collector and Superintendent of Police (SP) Vikrant Patil called for coordinated efforts by the police, education, excise, medical and welfare departments to make the district drug-free.

The Collector urged Education Department officials to conduct awareness programmes in all government and private schools, junior colleges and higher educational institutions. Students identified as drug users should be given confidential counselling and rehabilitation support. Officials were also told to identify school dropouts and prevent them from falling into drug abuse.

articles.title: Banana festival to showcase rare varieties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: To promote the diversity of indigenous bananas, their cultivation and associated food culture, Sahaja Samrudha, in collaboration with the Department of Horticulture, Karnataka State Agricultural Produce Processing and Export Corporation Limited (KAPPEC), ICAR–JSS Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Suttur, and Abhay Naturals, is organising a Banana Festival on November 14 and 15 at Nanjaraja Bahadur Choultry in Mysuru.

The two-day Banana Festival will be inaugurated by Venkataramana Reddy J. Patil, managing director, Karnataka State Agricultural Produce Processing and Export Corporation Limited (KAPPEC). Giridhar Parvatam, director of CSIR–Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysuru, will launch the Banana Bharat mobile application.

More than 150 banana varieties will be showcased at the festival. Visitors can purchase fresh bananas of several traditional varieties, including Nanjangud Rasabale, Nendran, Elakki Bale, Finger Banana, Kamalapur Red Banana, Karpuravalli, Poovan, Chandra Bale, Madarangi and Red Banana. Quality banana planting materials will also be available for those interested in cultivating bananas.

Daya Prasad from Sullia, who has conserved around 400 banana varieties, will bring some rare varieties from his collection for public display. Ram Prasad Hegde from Sirsi, a national award-winning plant conservationist, will also showcase rare banana varieties and planting materials. An eight-foot-long Sahasra Bale and a red banana variety whose entire plant appears as though it has been set on fire will be among the major attractions of the festival, according to press release.

A training programme on banana cultivation and opportunities for value addition will be held at 2:00 p.m on Saturday. At 10:30 am on Sunday, a children’s drawing competition and a banana-based cooking competition will be organised. Interested participants can take part. For more information, contact Ashok – 9632770473.

articles.title: Collectors to closely monitor comprehensive land resurvey: Ponguleti
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy directed district Collectors to closely monitor the comprehensive land resurvey and take an active role in resolving land-related issues at the field level.

At a video conference with Collectors, Additional Collectors, Revenue Divisional Officers and Survey Department officials on Wednesday, the Minister asked Collectors to visit villages regularly, interact with farmers and explain the survey process and the mechanism available for raising objections after the completion of the survey.

He directed officials to conduct public announcements in villages once every 15 days after issuing notices, so that landowners were aware of the opportunity to register their objections. Officials should also immediately communicate the extent of land recorded in revenue records and the extent established through the resurvey to the respective landowners, he said.
Mr. Srinivasa Reddy said Palair constituency had been selected as a pilot project, with the resurvey being taken up in all 141 revenue villages under its jurisdiction.

The Minister said the government had already issued a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the exercise, but variations in its implementation had been reported from different areas. Based on feedback, the SOP would be suitably modified.

He said a recent meeting with field officials from Siddipet, Medak and Sangareddy districts had focused on discrepancies in land extent, government lands and other disputes in villages where the survey had been completed or notices issued.

While appreciating the performance of the Collectors of Nalgonda and Khammam districts in conducting the resurvey, he expressed dissatisfaction with the progress in Nizamabad and asked the officials concerned to improve their performance and expedite the exercise in line with the targets.

Expressing concern over the continued pendency of issues relating to lands listed under Section 22-A, he said the government had already issued clear instructions on resolving them. Collectors should take special initiative to examine individual cases at the field level. Revenue Secretary D.S. Lokesh Kumar and Housing Secretary V.P. Gautam were present.

articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Benjamin Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Donald Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected accusations that Israel has been delaying the entry of winter supplies into the Gaza Strip as the enclave faces worsening conditions this week, with severe rains flooding makeshift tents.
He said Israel was not to blame for the worsening conditions for Palestinians in Gaza's tent camps that have been hit by severe winter floods.

His remarks came after the U.S.-created Board of Peace — established under U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Israel-Hamas war and oversee Gaza's recovery — said Monday (November 9, 2026) that Israel's delaying of the entry of winter supplies into Gaza had “exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge”.

Torrential rain has battered the war-torn enclave in recent days, damaging tens of thousands of makeshift tents. Four people, including three children, were killed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) when a large sandstone slab collapsed onto tents during the rains.

Mr. Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Mr. Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.
“Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza, and it is now cynically exploiting that suffering to shift blame onto Israel once again,” he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the situation in Gaza was “intolerable” and demanded Israel end “arbitrary restrictions” on aid. And in Washington, Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, the top Democrat on the Senate's foreign spending subcommittee, called for Israel to immediately allow winter gear into Gaza.

“There are a lot of challenges when it comes to Israel and Palestine that are complicated, and fraught, and contentious,” Mr. Schatz said on the Senate floor on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “But we should all be able to agree that repairing torn tents and helping people to dry out, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”

articles.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Meta told the Court last month it had adopted ​measures to ensure equal treatment of ‌the two campaigns

Brazil's electoral authority fined Meta's Facebook 7.5 million reais ($1.34 million) for failing to fully comply ​with judicial orders during last month's Presidential election runoff campaign, but said there ‌was no evidence so far that the company had ​deliberately acted to influence the outcome.

In a unanimous decision, ⁠the country's top electoral court (TSE) ruled on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that Facebook had failed to adequately meet court demands related to allegations that its ‌platform treated content from the rival campaigns of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator ‌Flavio Bolsonaro differently.

articles.title: Central committee suggests three-year roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand mining from active river channels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems

The Supreme Court-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) has suggested preparing a time-bound roadmap to phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years.

The committee, a statutory body since 2023 and originally formed in 2002 on the apex court's order, has also recommended developing sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.
For this, it has suggested scientific desiltation of dams and reservoirs and recycling of construction and demolition (C&D) waste, among other measures.
These recommendations are part of the CEC's report submitted to the Supreme Court on November 2 as part of a sou motu case related to illegal sand mining in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

In its report, the CEC observes that while sand and gravel are crucial ingredients for infrastructure and construction, their unscientific or excessive extraction from active channels and floodplains disrupts the delicate dynamic balance of river systems.

"The impacts inter alia include riverbed degradation and infrastructure vulnerability, depletion of groundwater and loss of aquifers, destruction of aquatic and riparian habitats, and alteration of river morphology and hydrology, etc," said the committee.
It also highlights that there is no consolidated, reliable national database that quantifies the volume or value of illegally extracted river sand.
As a result, the CEC has recommended strengthening the existing regulatory and monitoring framework governing extraction from permissible areas.

This can be done through scientific identification of mineable stretches, regular replenishment studies, determination of sustainable extraction limits, environmental safeguards, digital tracking of mineral transportation and end-use and effective enforcement, it said.

"A time-bound roadmap shall be prepared to progressively phase out unsustainable sand extraction from active river channels over the next three years, alongside development of adequate alternative sources, including reservoir sediment, M-sand and recycled C&D waste, while ensuring that legitimate construction requirements are met,” the CEC said in its report.

Moreover, the committee has said that there is an urgent need to develop sustainable alternative sources of sand and aggregates to progressively reduce dependence on extraction from active river channels.

"State governments shall promote the production and use of manufactured sand (M-Sand) through suitable incentives and quality certification, establish facilities for processing and recycling construction and demolition (C&D) waste into sand and aggregates, and permit recovery of sand and other materials from floodplains," suggested the CEC.

articles.title: Prix Pascal: If AI writes your book, are you still a writer?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: France’s new Prix Pascal for AI-assisted books prompts a writer to reflect on the slow pleasures of making art, loss of individuality, and need to reclaim human imagination

There is now a new French literary prize for AI-assisted writing — the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA. The Pascal prize requires entrants to turn in an unpublished manuscript, fiction or non-fiction, in French, of approximately 3,00,000 characters, written with the help of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Writers must declare which AI model and prompts they have employed. The applications, to be submitted by November 30, consist of “a seed, a manuscript and a technical file, submitted simultaneously”. Ten finalists will be announced on December 4 and the winner will be revealed on December 15.

“This [submitted] work must be useful, or raise awareness, or help to solve in an original way one of the ecological, social and ethical challenges that threaten humanity. AI can now solve previously unsolvable mathematical problems. Here, it is asked to produce a text that will help humanity progress towards wisdom and the preservation of itself and its environment.”

I love the way in which the manifesto strategically reframes tacit support for what goes against the very grain of the creative spirit as an essentially moral and ethical act. But of course! This is the way these things are usually done. The prize was founded by Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré. The first two are technology entrepreneurs, which too is no surprise.

Notwithstanding their precarity, writers and artists have always been viewed with a combination of envy, fear and hatred. The imagination is a dangerous thing. It is ungovernable. It cannot easily be controlled or colonised. It does not seek permission. And that, to many, is frightening. What better way to colonise the imagination than to introduce AI into the writer’s world? Also, that way everybody — even the ones with little understanding of what a writer does — can acquire the overnight label of one. Where does this leave writers who have spent years honing their craft, writers who have survived by the skin of their teeth? The world needs writers more urgently than ever before, and more of us should let some form of creative practice into our lives.

Two semesters ago, a few students from my Creative Writing course, at Shiv Nadar University, Chennai, confessed to what their worst fears were: that, having come of age in the post-AI era, they would find it a challenge to access and exercise their imagination — which, in their understanding, was foundational to the course. I was struck by their capacity for self-reflection, moved by what they recognised, quite rightly, as an imminent loss. This, too, is the other dark side of what we have got ourselves into: the loss of imagination is foundational not just to the stray creative writing course but to life itself.

The argument that it is best not to be left behind, that AI is here to stay so writers must take the good things it has to offer and navigate the rest, is a specious one. The folks making this argument may be right about the inevitability of AI, but does that make any of it less disturbing or a tad more ethical? I don’t see how one can frame this as anything other than a pure black-and-white story. If you give AI an inch, it is very likely that you will take a mile from yourself.

It is a slippery slope. You start by using AI as an instrument — perhaps to help you rewrite a sentence — and before you know it, you are likely to seek its help extensively to write the entire piece. Who then is the real author of the piece? After all, it is in the writing that writers do their thinking. I don’t think the answer lies in declaring AI use upfront. While this may address the ethical question to a small extent, it still does not change the fact that we are always going to ‘writing’ with training wheels on. The craft is in the writing and if you give that away what is left?

There is another problem too: that of the asymmetry between the writer on whose work an LLM is trained and the user who then draws on that work to write in “collaboration with” that particular AI model. The original writer whose consent has very likely not been sought gets nothing from this entire process — a process which de-humanises creative work and repurposes it as training data.

Artificial intelligence illustrations are seen on a lapto with books in the background in this illustration photo on 18 July, 2023. (Photo by Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | Photo Credit: Getty Images

As almost everyone from editors of literary journals on the brink of closure to writing teachers will tell you, it is often impossible to tell AI-assisted writing apart from human writing. In fact, you may find that some AI-assisted writing may be as good as if not better than writing by humans. It, of course, depends on the prompts used and how advanced the models are.

The LLMs have been trained to mimic human syntax, and because humans frequently edit AI text or may even adopt AI-like phrasing, it is impossible to be absolutely certain which is which. Neither dedicated AI-detection tools nor human readers are able to establish clearly whether a piece of writing is AI-generated or authored by a human. Worse still, detection tools often throw up false positives. This is especially true when it comes to non-native English writing. There are also ways to bypass detectors. OpenAI, however, discontinued its own native AI detection tool in 2023 because of low accuracy rates.

We are often told that AI-assisted text tends to exhibit certain stylistic patterns such as the em dash — which, incidentally, I use a lot — that you will find in it the overuse of certain words such as “delve” and parallel contrast structures such as “It is not just X, it is Y” or that it lacks “soul”. All these arguments were used in the controversy over Jamir Nazir’s 2026 Granta-Commonwealth Short Story Prize-winning entry “The Serpent in the Grove”.

articles.title: New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.
Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.
This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.
“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.

By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.
An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.

Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.

The key features of the proposed regulations include standardised criteria and procedures for provisional registration; online application, verification and issuance of registration certificates with unique identification numbers; provisions for validity, extension, termination and appeals relating to provisional registration; bridge courses for skill enhancement, competency assessments and qualifying exams; supervised clinical training and institutional requirements for professional skill development; and transition to regular registration in the appropriate Central or State Register.

New registration framework proposed to strengthen allied and healthcare professions in India

National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions invites public and stakeholder comments on the Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026

The National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Union Ministry of Health, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the registration of allied and healthcare professionals, with pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment, and transition to regular registration.

The broad categories of allied and healthcare professions governed by the NCAHP include clinical laboratories, surgical and emergency technology, physiotherapy, nutrition, ophthalmology, occupational therapy, community and behavioural health, medical imaging, physician associates, and health informatics.

The proposed framework aims for uniformity, transparency and accountability in professional registration. Practitioners can enhance their competencies in keeping with prescribed standards, a release issued by the Ministry said.

Key features of the proposed regulations include the establishment of a standardised mechanism for provisional registration in accordance with the NCAHP Act, 2021.

“Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable, to meet the requirements for regular registration,’’ the Healthy Ministry’s statement said.

This competency-based approach seeks to facilitate professional development and career progression, and improve the quality of allied and healthcare services.

“The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability,’’ a senior Health Ministry official said.

By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed requirements, the regulations seek to ensure allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.

An integrated online registration system for submitting applications, verifying credentials, assess eligibility, and issue provisional registration certificates is also proposed.

Eligible professionals granted provisional registration will receive a Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID). The digital platform will simply procedures, improve access, and promote uniform efficiency across States and Union Territories.

The key features of the proposed regulations include standardised criteria and procedures for provisional registration; online application, verification and issuance of registration certificates with unique identification numbers; provisions for validity, extension, termination and appeals relating to provisional registration; bridge courses for skill enhancement, competency assessments and qualifying exams; supervised clinical training and institutional requirements for professional skill development; and transition to regular registration in the appropriate Central or State Register.

articles.title: German military to stop using Chinese-made drones, citing security concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes; they will now be replaced with European products

Germany's military will no longer use Chinese-made drones, ​a defence ministry spokesperson said on Wednesday, amid mounting concern ‌among Western militaries that they could pose a ​security risk and be used to transmit ⁠sensitive information to Beijing.

Drones from Chinese manufacturers had previously been permitted as a cost-effective option for target practice and training purposes, ‌the spokesperson said. They will now be replaced with European products.
"To strengthen the Bundeswehr's ‌self-sufficiency and technological sovereignty, Chinese-made models will no ‌longer ⁠be used," the spokesperson said in an emailed ⁠statement.

There is no blanket ban on the use of systems from specific countries, the spokesperson said, adding the decision is based on ​individual risk assessments ‌aimed at safeguarding military security, IT and data security.
China's foreign ministry told Reuters that it opposed Germany's "discriminatory practice" targeting Chinese products.
Germany's Der Spiegel news outlet first ‌reported the change.

Local commanders had been allowed ​to purchase the drones under a 2024 strategy that included a "white list" of approved systems, ⁠including several made by China-based DJI, the world's largest drone maker, Spiegel reported.

DJI has repeatedly said its ‌drones do not pose a security risk and in May the company told US lawmakers that an independent review had found "no evidence of data transmission outside the United States".

The US last month prohibited vehicles made by China's BYD on its air base on Japan's ‌Okinawa island, and Poland in February banned Chinese-made vehicles from ​military facilities over concerns their sensors could be used to collect sensitive data.

The spokesperson said the ⁠German defence ministry had no general ban on vehicles from ⁠specific countries or manufacturers, but said sensors installed in modern vehicles are seen as potential security ‌risks, and therefore access to sensitive military sites can be restricted where necessary.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier

The Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), as armed conflict hampers the response.
The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC's history was officially declared in May, but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier.
It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health.
Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever.
Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years.
The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020.
The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu.
Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.
No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak.

Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.
Security in eastern DRC is another challenge in fighting the health crisis.
Ituri province is one of the most volatile and clashes between armed groups and violence against health workers regularly occur.

articles.title: Italy evacuates over 300 schools due to bomb alert, with threats in Scotland and Ireland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said there was no indication of any “concrete danger” to schools and that the threats appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern”

Italian authorities evacuated hundreds of schools on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after an emailed bomb threat, the latest in a series of disruptions affecting European institutions following recent hoaxes aimed at airlines and broadcasters.
Schools in Ireland, Scotland and Northern Ireland received similar threats, but no evacuations were reported.

Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni said there was no indication of any “concrete danger” to schools and that the threats appeared aimed at “generating alarm and concern”. She said investigations were underway and that she had called a meeting of ministers for later Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

The anonymous email also threatened Ms. Meloni, according to copies obtained by Italian media, including the LaPresse news agency. She did not address the personal threat in her statement, and her office had no immediate comment.

The email purported to come from the leader of an otherwise unknown group with an anti-woman name and contained particularly violent threats. It was signed with the same Russian name used in last week's threats against European broadcasters.
Authorities have not attributed the threats to any group or state, and no evidence has emerged linking the hoaxes to a government.

Police in Northern Ireland said they were conducting “urgent inquiries” after a threatening email was sent to hundreds of schools. Police in Scotland said they were treating similar messages as hoaxes and were not requiring schools to evacuate.
“Our assessment remains that they do not represent a credible threat,” Police Scotland said.
Police in Ireland also said they were aware of a “generic communication” sent to several educational institutions.
Italian Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara told reporters that 312 schools had been evacuated after receiving email threats.

“These are very delicate considerations, because there is always the risk that there is someone else behind the madman,” he said. “Given that so many schools are involved, the real risk is almost non-existent.”
At Rome's Mamiani high school, students poured into the streets, mistaking the alarm for the recess bell. They learned of the bomb threat only after they were outside.

articles.title: COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels

Wars and trade disputes should not be allowed to distract the world from ​its struggle to combat global warming, the leaders of Brazil and Turkey told the COP31 climate conference ⁠on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

"A year ago, the planet left COP30 invigorated... (but) this momentum has dropped off at the start of this year. Climate change disappeared from the speeches and documents from global leadership," Brazil's President Luiz ‌Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year's conference, told the summit.
"We started talking more about weapons ‌and ⁠tariffs than the survival of future generations," he said. "The planet cannot be in the mercy of ⁠hegemonic struggles."
"Wars, crises, migration, famine and poverty increase the need for international solidarity each day," he said.
The U.S. and Israeli war on Iran this year has disrupted West Asia crude oil shipments and sent fuel prices soaring around the ​globe, triggering a scramble for reliable supplies.

Those dynamics ‌have pushed global warming down the list of urgent priorities for some governments, even as climate advocates argue they make the perfect case for a more rapid adoption of clean energy alternatives to oil.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement at COP31 on a proposal from Turkey to increase the share of electricity in global ‌energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told ​world leaders earlier in the day that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction, and that fast action was needed to ⁠avert it.

"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction," Mr. Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters.

A UN report last month found ‌the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

Meanwhile, 2026 has also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a catastrophic flood killing more than 1,450 people, with thousands still missing.

Former French Prime Minister Laurent Fabius, who presided over the 2015 Paris climate conference and leads an advisory council of former COP presidents, said the leaders' speeches should give political impetus to the ‌negotiations.

articles.title: ‘Iran will not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington

Iran will not allow even a single ​particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country, and there ‌will be consequences in the event of any ​new U.S. strikes on the Islamic Republic, Iranian ⁠security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in televised remarks.

Mr. Rezaei was speaking to Lebanon's pro-Iranian Al Mayadeen TV after U.S. officials downplayed the need ‌for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the ‌Republicans' defeat in the November 3 midterm elections.
Mr. Rezaei has ‌said ⁠there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran ⁠and Washington.
"Any new U.S. attacks will also be met with targeting U.S. bases far away," he said.
Iran's Supreme Leader has issued a directive ​that the country's near-weapons-grade uranium ‌should not be sent abroad, two senior Iranian sources said in May.

"We need the enriched material to design ships and submarines that work on nuclear energy", Mr. Rezaei said, ‌adding that Tehran has informed Moscow that its enriched ​nuclear material will remain in the country and "we will use it ourselves".
Russia has previously offered to ⁠remove uranium from Iran as part of a potential deal to ease U.S. concerns, but said it was for Tehran to ‌decide whether to remove it or not.

The IAEA estimates that Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to 60% — a level far higher than needed for civilian use — when Israel and the U.S. attacked Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025. How much of that has survived is ‌unclear.
Israel, the United States and other Western countries have long accused Iran ​of seeking nuclear weapons. Iran denies the accusation.
Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of ⁠any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the war between the ⁠two countries.
Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only ‌after Washington meets seven demands which Tehran has presented, a senior Iranian official told Reuters last week.

articles.title: Navi Mumbai recognised as India’s cleanest city in latest Swachh Survekshan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Indore, ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the winners this year
Navi Mumbai has been adjudged the cleanest city in India at a central government awards programme, while Gujarat’s Surat was second and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh finished third.
Among cities with a population between three lakh and 10 lakh, Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain emerged as the cleanest urban centre, followed by the UT of Chandigarh and Guntur in Andhra Pradesh.
Indore, which had been ranked the cleanest city in the country for the past eight years, did not figure among the toppers this year.
The awards were presented by President Droupadi Murmu at an event held here.
Rewa, another city in Madhya Pradesh, emerged as the cleanest riverfront town, followed by Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) and Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) in second and third place, respectively.
In the 10 lakh-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam emerged as the cleanest city, followed by Jabalpur and Lucknow.
According to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, in the Swachh Coastal Town category, Puri in Odisha was ranked first, followed by Kerala’s Alappuzha and Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri.
Rudrapur, in Uttarakhand, emerged as the cleanest Himalayan city, while Jammu secured the second position.
Last year, Indore had topped the league, followed by Surat and Navi Mumbai. Jaipur was recognised as the cleanest city in Rajasthan, while Gwalior received the distinction in Madhya Pradesh.

Swachh Survekshan is Swacch Bharat Mission-Urban’s flagship cleanliness assessment, with the goal of improving urban sanitation, hygiene, and waste management. Over 4,751 cities participated in the latest edition.

Swachh Survekshan made several key enhancements for the 2025-26 awards, including greater emphasis on citizen feedback, expanded coverage of Urban River Fronts, Coastlines and Water bodies and focused indicators on prevention of open defecation and open urination, cleanliness of tourist and heritage hotspots, and behaviour change initiatives in schools.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

articles.title: Young and fast: on F1’s youngest champion
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

As F1’s youngest champion, Kimi Antonelli can attract a new generation of fans

Andrea Kimi Antonelli etched his name in motorsport history by becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One World Championship . The 20-year-old has secured his maiden title with four races to spare after finishing third at the Mexico Grand Prix on Sunday. The Italian’s feat is remarkable, for he has claimed the crown in his sophomore campaign, becoming only the fifth driver in history to do so in the first or second season. Mercedes signed Antonelli for its junior driver programme when he was just 12. Since then, the Italian’s step towards F1 has been meticulously managed. After acing the F4 championships, Antonelli skipped one level to transition to F2. And when the opportunity arose to fill a seat vacated by seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff took a bold gamble by drafting in the youngster. Antonelli’s rookie campaign in 2025 was baptism by fire, and he was outclassed by teammate George Russell. For 2026, F1 ushered in drastic changes with new engine and aerodynamic regulations, dramatically altering the dynamics of the cars. Though conventional wisdom suggested that the experienced Russell would be the favourite, the Italian prodigy embraced the challenge astonishingly well. This was best exemplified by how he won five consecutive races starting from the second round of the season.

One of the hardest things in F1 is handling the nerves associated with protecting the lead, especially when it is the driver’s first attempt at a Championship bid. Antonelli, though, was incredibly consistent throughout the year, and hardly made any errors. Titles are often decided by how a driver minimises his losses on bad days, and Antonelli showed great temperament in this regard. At the same time, he was ruthless on the track and made decisive overtaking manoeuvres. The defining race was in Monza, Italy, in September, where Antonelli charged from 19th on the grid to win his home Grand Prix, finishing ahead of Russell who started second. It was a statement of intent, and strengthened his grip on the trophy. Drivers often raise their games following a world title, more so when success comes early in their career. Considering the giant leap Antonelli made to become F1’s first champion to be born in the 21st century, he will undoubtedly attract a new generation of fans. The charm of the sport lies in its iconic driver rivalries such as Ayrton Senna versus Alain Prost, and Michael Schumacher versus Mika Hakkinen. With four-time champion Max Verstappen widely considered the gold standard of the present era, Antonelli could well be the perfect candidate to battle the Dutchman in F1’s next great rivalry.

articles.title: Trump debacle: On the U.S. midterm election results
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Democrats must use their win to influence policy and improve lives

President Donald Trump faced the worst political setback of his current term in office after the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the mid-term election. Democrats not only won resoundingly in their traditional stronghold States, such as Colorado, Oregon and Illinois, and held onto important swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan and Virginia, but they also made historic inroads into “red states” such as Texas, Kansas and Iowa. While Mr. Trump fumed that Republicans would have performed better had his name been on the ballot, he also appeared to be resigned to the imminent reality of working with Democratic lawmakers over the remaining two years of his administration. Beyond the immediate impact on the future functioning of the federal government, this week’s “bluenami” has also brought sweeping changes at the State level: Democrats won a Senate seat in Texas for the first time in 37 years; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won in Michigan , making him the first Muslim Senator in history ; Chris Pappas of New Hampshire became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate ; and Senate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries will soon be the first African-American Speaker of the House.
Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

It is ironic that Mr. Trump alluded to his name not being on the ballot as the cause for the Republican collapse because, for many voters, the midterm election was indeed a referendum on the second Trump administration’s performance in office. The result has been an unambiguous thumbs-down from voters so far as top policy areas of the Trump administration are concerned, including cost of living and jobs, immigration enforcement, the war in Iran. The writing was on the wall, as were the approval ratings, especially in the case of oil prices and the Iran war, given that the price of gas in the U.S. has soared since the conflict around the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Similarly, the widespread raids by ICE and accelerated deportation processes for undocumented migrants led to protests across States and galvanised progressives around immigration reform. While Democrats may be justified in celebrating their victory after two years of harsh Trumpism, they would do well to remember that the President still retains a veto vote for policies passed by Congress. The temptation to launch a series of investigations and interrogate the functioning of the Trump White House may be strong, yet congressional Democrats may wish to avoid any posturing that yields no palpable policy impact, including kicking off impeachment proceedings against Mr. Trump. A more productive way forward for Democratic lawmakers would be to engage with the White House and, through negotiation and compromise, mitigate the real impact of deleterious policies in critical areas such as health-care insurance and tariffs.

articles.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must eliminate situations that lead to sewer cleaning deaths

Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. In 2025, there was an order to end manual sewer cleaning in four metropolitan cities, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad followed a year later with notices to 15 Chief Secretaries for disobeying the 2023 order, including on the compensation.

Private contractors and municipal bodies are known to violate the restrictions on manual cleaning specified in the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act 2013 and Rules, and evade liability by hiring undocumented daily-wage workers. The scourge of such worker deaths thus cannot be eliminated without also formalising their employment and improving social security across caste lines. A significant gap between aims and outcomes has also persisted under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem scheme . And while it is centred on urban local bodies, its difficulties speak to the state’s fundamental error: to maximise administrative assistance, such as by distributing kits, rather than minimising the number of situations that could lead to worker deaths.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

articles.title: Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The world must act on Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities

Briefing the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last week on the International Commission of Inquiry’s latest report on the situation in Israel and the Palestinian territories , its chairperson, retired Indian judge Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, did not couch his words in ambiguity. He said that the unequivocal conclusion was that Israeli security forces continued to commit “war crimes, crimes against humanity, and the crime of genocide” a year after the October 2025 ceasefire agreement brokered by the U.S. The Commission’s third such submission since October 7, 2023, the report focuses on the “killings and bodily and mental harm by state actors”, predominantly Israeli security forces. It draws on medical records, satellite imagery, forensic analysis, witness testimony and videos posted by Israeli soldiers. Despite Israeli denials, the report finds that soldiers targeted Palestinian civilians, including infants, by using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to identify and execute their targets with impunity ; the report quotes top Israel officials claiming the killings. Justice Muralidhar said that more than 75,000 Palestinians including 21,500 children and 11,000 women have been killed across Palestinian territories since 2023 , and yet “little or no action” is being taken by member-states, including Israel itself. The report calls on UN members to “employ all means” to prevent the genocide, investigate and prosecute suspects for it, and establish clear rules for AI use in conflicts. The Committee had previously called on UN members to halt military transfers to Israel , and pass sanctions against those linked to child abuses, as well as to cooperate with the International Criminal Court to enforce arrest warrants against Israeli officials and soldiers.

The committee’s findings have shocked many around the world but have not thus far effected much action. The UNGA lacks the power to implement any resolution aimed at preventing Israel’s actions, and the UN Security Council lacks the consensus to do so, given the U.S.’s support of Israel. So, it should come as no surprise that Justice Muralidhar could not even present the report to the UNGA in person, as the U.S. withheld grant of a visa. New Delhi, while upholding Palestinian rights and providing humanitarian aid, has avoided any recommendation that could harm relations with Israel. India has abstained from UN resolutions calling for a ceasefire or action against Israel , while continuing to supply it with arms, ammunition, ordnance and drone parts. The Ministry of External Affairs has neither directly criticised Israel’s actions nor commented on the disturbing findings of reports by the UN commission chaired by Justice Muralidhar and his predecessor, 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navanethem Pillay . The government’s silence is in conflict with its stated principles and could place it on the wrong side of history.

articles.title: Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: India is ready to mediate to establish grain safety agreement for “food corridors”, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy

India is ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish “food corridors”, announced Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcoming the offer after a telephone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of the Ukraine-Russia peace talks set to begin in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday. Mr. Modi conveyed India’s “readiness” to help with all initiatives to end the nearly five-year-old conflict. The call was followed by another call between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump’s negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, will restart negotiations after three months with Russian and Ukrainian representatives to discuss security guarantees required for a possible ceasefire. The calls from New Delhi came just ahead of the talks in the UAE, and a week before Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the ASEAN-linked summits in Manila. Later this month, Mr. Trump is expected to travel to Shenzhen for the APEC summit in China, that Russian President Vladimir Putin is also expected to attend, making the timing of the Modi-Zelenskyy and Jaishankar-Lavrov calls more significant.

“Prime Minister [Modi] reaffirmed India’s human-centric approach and reiterated India’s consistent position that the conflict must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy,” the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement about the Modi-Zelenskyy call. “He conveyed India’s readiness to contribute to all efforts aimed at peaceful resolution of the conflict,” it added.

In a post on social media, Mr. Zelenskyy said he had briefed Mr. Modi on the latest developments and stressed that Mr. Modi had said to Mr. Putin that the war must end. The Ukrainian President said Russia must understand that the “global economy and hundreds of millions of people around the world are suffering because of blocked sea routes” in the Black Sea, and called for India to clarify its peace proposal.

“It is important that India identify what steps it can take and what dialogue it can pursue with other leaders to help bring the war to an end. Food security could be one such area. We discussed Russia’s blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea. India is ready to mediate in establishing food corridors, and we are counting on these efforts to continue,” Mr. Zelenskyy wrote.

Within a couple of hours of the announcement, Mr. Jaishankar posted that he had spoken to his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov as well, and said their conversation had “focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives”. Mr. Jaishankar, who has been discussing India’s proposals on a grain export agreement or a food corridor in the Black Sea, on the safety of sea mariners, and safe passage for energy shipments with both countries, had first disclosed the initiatives during a visit to Poland and Ukraine in September. On October 22, during the visit of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to Delhi, Indian officials had said it had reached out to both Russian and Ukrainian governments with a “four-point proposal” for an agreement that would stop attacks on civilians, allow grain and energy exports from both countries through the Black Sea, and end the targeting of ships and seafarers, many of whom are Indian nationals. Highly placed officials had told The Hindu that New Delhi was in close contact with both sides over the specific proposal, and the government had hoped to hear back from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides at the earliest. With talks set to begin on Tuesday, it remains to be seen whether India will join the dialogue already in play with the U.S. and the UAE, or whether New Delhi plans a larger role in mediating or hosting talks between Russia and Ukraine in the future.

Mr. Modi conveyed India’s “readiness” to help with all initiatives to end the nearly five-year-old conflict. The call was followed by another call between External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Within a couple of hours of the announcement, Mr. Jaishankar posted that he had spoken to his Russian counterpart Mr. Lavrov as well, and said their conversation had “focused on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing diplomatic initiatives”. Mr. Jaishankar, who has been discussing India’s proposals on a grain export agreement or a food corridor in the Black Sea, on the safety of sea mariners, and safe passage for energy shipments with both countries, had first disclosed the initiatives during a visit to Poland and Ukraine in September. On October 22, during the visit of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to Delhi, Indian officials had said it had reached out to both Russian and Ukrainian governments with a “four-point proposal” for an agreement that would stop attacks on civilians, allow grain and energy exports from both countries through the Black Sea, and end the targeting of ships and seafarers, many of whom are Indian nationals. Highly placed officials had told The Hindu that New Delhi was in close contact with both sides over the specific proposal, and the government had hoped to hear back from both the Russian and Ukrainian sides at the earliest. With talks set to begin on Tuesday, it remains to be seen whether India will join the dialogue already in play with the U.S. and the UAE, or whether New Delhi plans a larger role in mediating or hosting talks between Russia and Ukraine in the future.

articles.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The deceased were identified as a staff nurse and four inmates of a government-recognised children’s home for girls
A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area.

On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned.

Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered.

Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way.

articles.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab.

Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity.
The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1.
Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts.

A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said.
The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone.

In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. The SDRF, with the coordination of Dial-112 rescued 40 passengers travelling in a bus stranded in floodwaters in Srikakulam. In another incident, the personnel assisted in rescuing eight fishermen caught in danger due to the cyclone, the officers said.
The DGP appreciated the courage, dedication, and commitment of the APSDRF in saving the lives of people during disasters, stating that their services are a matter of pride for the Police Department.
He presented rewards to officers and personnel who exhibited outstanding bravery in rescue and relief operations during the cyclone.

articles.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led government enjoys public goodwill despite concerns about it being directionless
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an ‘empty coffer,’ the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures

The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government, which completed six months in office on Monday (November 9, 2026), appears to be largely enjoying the goodwill of people, even though concerns are being raised about the regime’s tendency to be directionless.

Though Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an “empty coffer,” the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures. The “precarious” financial condition did not come in the way of his government carrying out some other steps such as the extension of the breakfast scheme for school students, the provision of gold rings to babies born at government hospitals, the distribution of eight-gram gold coins and silk saris to eligible women, and the expansion of free travel for women on buses of the State Transport Corporations.

Reports of a “marked reduction“ in corruption regarding government appointments, transfers, and public services have impressed many observers including former Union Minister P. Chidambaram and UN diplomat-turned-political writer R. Kannan. In an interview with this newspaper a couple of months ago, Mr. Chidambaram stated: “I also understand that sanctions for the appointment of teachers in [government-aided] schools and colleges have been sent by post.” According to Mr. Kannan, “transparency remains the Vijay administration’s strongest asset.” The ruling party’s national spokesperson, Americai V. Narayanan, says: “He [Mr. Vijay] does not do things to please others or earn applause. He does them because he genuinely believes in them. In politics, where symbolism often outweighs conviction, that distinction matters.”

Notwithstanding the general perception about the government‘s integrity, the two Dravidian majors — the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) — have been unsparing. One of the areas of their attack is on the power front, where the current regime had, ironically, begun with the increase in the quantum of free power to 200 units bimonthly to domestic consumers subject to the overall consumption not exceeding 500 units. The regime’s plans for power purchase on a short-term basis at a higher cost has raised questions about the government’s competence.

DMK president M.K. Stalin and AIADMK’s Amma Peravai secretary R.B. Udhayakumar wondered when Keralam could buy electricity at lower price, why Tamil Nadu has not been able to procure at comparable rates. Besides, even the lower price has triggered a controversy in the neighbouring State.

It is not only on the power front where the government is found on a weak wicket but also on many other policy matters. On the issue of wooing industrial investment, the Opposition’s attack has not been firmly rebutted by the government. As for the TVK regime’s project of building a new Secretariat complex, there has not been any categorical statement from the Chief Minister on the controversy triggered by it, though his Ministerial colleagues, at times, make different observations.

“The new government often appears directionless, evidenced by hasty decision-making and conspicuous silence on controversial issues,“ Mr. Kannan observes. He adds that moving forward, the priority must shift from perpetual campaigning to effective governance.

A senior citizen, who calls himself a “well wisher“ of the ruling party, points out that “a structured, periodic forum for district and block-level leaders would help. Without it, the party could pay a price in the forthcoming local body elections.”

Even as the TVK government faces a host of challenges in sustained governance, it is also expected to fulfil its key electoral promises such as the increase in the monthly assistance for women to ₹2,500.
