articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait

The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: the hurdles, the risks and the politics | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it

The story so far: Sheikh Hasina sought a new passport and a national identity card from the Government of Bangladesh on Monday (November 9, 2026). In response, Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said that Bangladesh seeks her extradition under an “acceptable prisoner transfer process”. This is the latest episode in the Hasina saga that began when she came to India on August 5, 2024, after the student-people uprising toppled her government.

Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it. How to return to face justice and yet emerge as a leader of her country is the big challenge before her. She has refused to apologise for the crackdown, saying the police did not take her orders but responded to angry agitators and militants who had provoked them.

Global & Diplomatic Brief: Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: the hurdles, the risks and the politics | Explained. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and proactive engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

Geopolitical Significance: Strengthening strategic partnerships across the Indo-Pacific, Global South, and multilateral forums such as the UN, G20, BRICS, and SCO remains central to India's foreign policy.

articles.title: U.S.-brokered talks are set to start in Abu Dhabi to discuss Ukraine-Russia peace deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees

The three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States start on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) in the United Arab Emirates, renewing a push for peace after several rounds of negotiations earlier this year.

The two-day session in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February, will focus on security guarantees. U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a "negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment.”
Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal to end the full-scale war, now nearing its five-year mark .

Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow illegally annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.

Mr. Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejects Mr. Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia has not been able to take on the battlefield. Mr. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.

Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.

Russia's chief negotiator is Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who has led Moscow's team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul, Turkey, in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff's operational department Yuri Zhigarlovsky.

Ukraine's delegation is led by Rustem Umerov, head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service, who also attended earlier talks. It also reportedly includes Mr. Zelenskyy's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy Sergiy Kyslytsya and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Mr. Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.

articles.title: G7 attention in Paris turns to Ukraine while U.S.-mediated talks get underway in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: It was not immediately clear if the U.S. or any of its G7 partners would announce any new assistance for Ukraine

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his counterparts from the Group of 7 developed democracies are turning their attention toward Ukraine and how to support it in its struggle to defend itself from Russia. As three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States get underway in the United Arab Emirates, top G7 diplomats are meeting on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with Ukraine's foreign minister in France.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha will start his day in Paris in talks with Mr. Rubio before heading to the French Foreign Ministry for a larger group meeting with the entire G7. They will discuss defense and security assistance to Ukraine, which President Donald Trump's administration has reduced, causing consternation not only in Kyiv but in capitals across Europe, the largest of which — Paris, Berlin, Rome and London — are G7 members.
It was not immediately clear if the U.S. or any of its G7 partners would announce any new assistance for Ukraine.

Meanwhile, in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will be meeting Russian and Ukrainian officials in part to persuade Moscow to agree to broader negotiations that would include key European officials on how to end nearly five years of war.

In Paris, Europeans have been clamouring for a seat at the table in Abu Dhabi, but two US officials said Monday that representatives from Britain, Germany, France, NATO and the European Union would not join the main talks but rather discuss potential security guarantees and the long-term security architecture between Russia and Europe beforehand.

Russia has resisted European participation in negotiations and insisted the talks should proceed strictly as a trilateral format involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States. The three last held talks in February.
But on Monday (November 9) in Paris, German Foreign Minister Johan Wadephul, who met separately with Rubio on the sidelines of the G7, was emphatic that Europe must be included.

“I am still very grateful to the United States of America for making every effort to get the parties to the conflict to the table,” he said. “But I made clear again here that Europe belongs at this table. There can be no solution without Europe, only with Europe.”
Mr. Rubio said the U.S. has no objection to eventual European involvement in the direct talks, but that it wasn't yet time.

“Ultimately, it would be a positive, but we've got a ways to go,” he told reporters after a full day of group and bilateral meetings with G7 counterparts. “But, no, it's good that they're talking, it's good that the trilateral talks are on again. It's better than not having talks.”
On the eve of the talks, Russia battered Ukraine's power grid again on Monday (November 9), and Ukrainian forces hit another of Russia's biggest oil refineries.

The two countries remain locked in battle with no sign that either side is ready to budge from their demands. The war has already killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians, analysts and humanitarian organizations say.

articles.title: UFC chief Dana White declines Donald Trump's White House job offer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Dana White visited the White House on November 9, and Donald Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White turned down President Donald Trump's -- apparently jovial -- offer of a job as press secretary in a surprise appearance at the White House on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Mr. Trump stunned the world by saying on social media on Saturday (November 7) that he had asked Mr. White to take on the high-profile post -- but a day later the 80-year-old president said he was "only kidding."
The 57-year-old cage fighting boss visited the White House on Monday (November 9), and Mr. Trump brought him out for a chaotic news conference in the James Brady Briefing Room.
"So let me ask you the big question. Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America? Or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC? Huh?" Mr. Trump said.
"Thank you for the offer, sir -- for the offer, I have no, no -- I do not want to be in politics," Mr. White replied.
Trump smiled and headed out of the room, saying: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everybody."

The press secretary's post has been been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week in the post. Her combative predecessor Karoline Leavitt left in August after a year and a half in the job.

Mr. Trump's announcement that he had offered the high-profile job to "violent Fighter and Warrior" Mr. White had sparked speculation that he was ready for a aggressive stance after the Republican Party's stunning midterm elections defeat.
Mr. White is a long-time friend of the president and helped host a massive UFC match on the White House lawn earlier this year.
But there was also some scepticism about the president's announcement, and Mr. Trump said Sunday (November 8) night that he had been joking.
Leading out Mr. White to the podium on Monday (November 9), Mr. Trump said he had been "having a little fun."
"He's a great guy," Mr. Trump told the room full of reporters. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you."

articles.title: Bill in U.S. Congress to recognise Deepavali as federal holiday, 19 lawmakers back proposal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: If the Bill is passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the 12th federally recognised holiday in the United States
A group of U.S. lawmakers, led by Grace Meng, on Monday (November 9, 2026) said they will re-introduce a bill in the House of Representatives to recognise Deepavali as a federal holiday.

Ms. Meng, the chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), and 19 U.S. lawmakers, including Raja Krishnamoorthi, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Ro Khanna and Ami Bera, re-introduced the Deepavali Day Act to recognise the festival as a federal holiday.

“My Diwali Day Act will help educate Americans about the importance of this day, and I will continue working to create a more inclusive nation that honours the rich cultural traditions of its people,” Ms. Meng said in a statement.

The draft legislation describes Diwali, also known as Deepavali or the Festival of Lights, as one of the most important holidays of the year for many religious groups including Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists as well as billions in the South Asian, Southeast Asian and Indo-Caribbean communities.

Ms. Meng said while the celebration holds a different significance for these diverse religious, ethnic and cultural groups, the Festival of Lights unites those who observe with reflection, prayer and gathering with loved ones.

“Diwali represents the triumph of good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. At a time when anti-Hindu and anti-South Asian hate is on the rise, recognising Diwali as a federal holiday sends a powerful message that Hindus, as well as Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists, are valued members of our society,” Ms. Meng said.
Hindu and South Asian communities across the country are facing an alarming rise in hate, intimidation, and targeted violence, a CAPAC statement said.

“This includes vandalism at Hindu places of worship, an attempted mass shooting during Navratri festivities at a Hindu temple in Illinois, and the recent racist disruption of a Diwali celebration in Washington State. CAPAC has been sounding the alarm that these acts of hate must be taken seriously and investigated by federal authorities,” it said.
If the Bill is passed by Congress, Deepavali would become the 12th federally recognised holiday in the United States.
Establishing a federal holiday for Deepavali, and the day off it would provide, would demonstrate that the government values the rich cultures and traditions of its citizens.
Ms. Meng is also the author of the Lunar New Year Day Act, which would establish Lunar New Year as a federally recognised holiday.

The Bill is also endorsed by Asian Americans Advancing Justice (AAJC), Asian American Federation (AAF), Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA), Hindus for Human Rights, Hindu Temple Society of North America, Indian American Impact, Indian Diaspora Council, Indo-Caribbean Alliance, International Commission on Dalit Rights, National Asian Pacific American Bar Association (NAPABA), National Council of Asian Pacific Americans (NCAPA), OCA-Asian Pacific American Advocates, Sikh American Legal Defense and Education Fund (SALDEF), The Sikh Cultural Society, The Sikh Coalition, South Asian Impact Foundation, and Southeast Asia Resource Action Center (SEARAC).

articles.title: How AI is reshaping China’s universities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: AI disruption and a tightening job market are driving a sweeping change across China’s universities; under the government’s ‘guideline on the reform of higher education institutions’, universities will now be tasked with specific goals, pursuing either research, application-oriented objectives, or skills development

In September 2026, China’s government unveiled an ambitious 10-year plan to reform its universities. Driving the change is an increasingly challenging job market for the country’s close to 13 million college graduates, who are facing the twin disruptions of AI and a slowing economy. Under the plan, dozens of graduate programmes are being disbanded, while universities themselves will be categorised and tasked with either pursuing research, applications or skills development.

A combination of factors, some not too dissimilar to the current challenges in India’s own job market, has left policymakers grappling with a tepid job market and a vast number of graduates facing dim job prospects. Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

Under the plan, dozens of graduate programmes are being disbanded, while universities themselves will be categorised and tasked with either pursuing research, applications or skills development.
• A combination of factors, some not too dissimilar to the current challenges in India’s own job market, has left policymakers grappling with a tepid job market and a vast number of graduates facing dim job prospects. Top of the list is a mismatch in skills between graduates and what companies are seeking. Depressed economic sentiment has also led companies to cut back on hiring, with the prolonged structural slowdown in the real estate market dragging down growth. AI is the third disruptive force, changing rapidly how the marketplace views and values skills.

As he worked, he talked about the elephants he already knew: the ones that wandered into his village, damaged crops, and left people afraid. To him, elephants had always been something that showed up in human spaces uninvited.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship

Nvidia ​and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued on ‌Monday (November 9, 2026) in a proposed class action accusing ​them of defrauding shareholders by ⁠concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

According to a complaint filed in federal court ‌in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Huang's alleged affair with ‌Alice Huang, a former executive ‌of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed who is not related to ⁠him, and did not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened Nvidia's reputation and ​business prospects.
The New ‌York Times reported last month about the alleged relationship, and that U.S. authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence ‌asset.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment.
Jensen Huang told Nvidia's employees he had ⁠been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship.

He co-founded Nvidia and ‌has led the Santa Clara, California-based company as it became the world's most valuable chipmaker and made him one of the world's most prominent symbols of the artificial intelligence boom.

Nvidia announced a probe into ‌the matter on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Its shares closed down ​4.3% on Monday (November 9, 2026), reducing Nvidia's market capitalisation by approximately $190 billion. The lawsuit ⁠was filed five minutes after the U.S. stock ⁠market closed.
It is common for shareholders to sue companies after unexpected share ‌price declines. Nvidia shareholders, led by Mark Kistenmacher are seeking unspecified damages from ​the defendants.

articles.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.
The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions.
Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).
These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence.
ChatGPT's 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further.
With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia's market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion -- currently on par with Apple as the world's two most valuable companies.
Washington bans the export of Nvidia's top-end "Blackwell" and "Rubin" GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications.
The policy also allows the United States's top AI labs to maintain their global lead.
Huang has lobbied the U.S. government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives.
This year, Washington eased controls on Nvidia's previously banned -- and less powerful -- "H200" chip, with the United States taking a 25% cut of sales.
But U.S. conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum.
Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on U.S. rivals.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

The church sees the initiative as more than a fitness facility. “We want to groom a healthy generation. Many people suffer from lifestyle diseases, while youngsters often turn to private fitness centres. We felt that providing basic facilities here would benefit the community. Spirituality is also about nurturing a healthy mind and body. We consider this a form of spiritual service,” says assistant vicar Fr. Jees Akkara.

For Fr. Eluvathingal, there is another purpose. “Youngsters rarely come to church or participate in its activities these days. This is also an opportunity to bring more of them into the church community,” he says.

articles.title: Trump says FBI looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with 'Chinese agent'
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The sudden emergence of Nvidia CEO Huang's infidelity has created concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence

U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday (November 9, 2026) that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
“I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape,” Mr. Trump said at a White House briefing.

The sudden emergence of Mr. Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence.

Mr. Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Mr. Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Mr. Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

Mr. Huang -- a singular figure in the technology landscape and one of the world's wealthiest people -- has acknowledged that he had an affair, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.

“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security,” Mr. Huang said in his letter.
Nvidia announced Sunday (November 8, 2026) it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Mr. Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The episode is also attracting congressional scrutiny, with top Democrats Sen. Mark Warner and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries saying on Monday (November 9, 2026) that they are interested in investigating it further. Jeffries said the Nvidia issue came up during a closed-door session with the CIA director and the Director of National Intelligence that was primarily about Iran.

“We're going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened,” he said, “and what the implications are in terms of America's national security.”

Mr. Trump is slated to meet next week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but he was noncommittal about bringing up the situation with Mr. Xi.
“No, I don't think so,” Mr. Trump said. “I mean, maybe. I'm sure President XI will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he's a very honourable man.”

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. State Department formally serves notice on India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Department of State said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case

The U.S. State Department, through a diplomatic note, has formally served notice on the Government of India regarding Khalistan separatist Gurpatwant Pannun’s civil lawsuit over an alleged assassination plot.

The U.S. State Department said it was legally obliged to do so and is not taking a position on the case, adding, “The documents were delivered to the Embassy of India in Washington under cover of the U.S. Department of State note dated October 20, 2026. The diplomatic note was signed on September 30, 2026, and delivered on October 9, 2026.”

The U.S. State Department’s diplomatic note said “I, John Ballard Managing Director of the Directorate of Overseas Citizens Services, in Washington certify that this is a true copy of the United States Department of State diplomatic note signed on September 30, 2026 and delivered to the Embassy of the Republic of India in Washington DC on October 9, 2026.”

On February 16, 2026, Indian citizen Nikhil Gupta had pled “guilty” at a court in New York to charges of murder, conspiracy, and money laundering to assassinate Khalistani activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. The government is yet to comment on the case.

According to investigators in the United States, Mr. Gupta, an Indian businessman, worked with an Indian “government employee” Vikash Yadav, believed to have been associated with India’s external intelligence agency R&AW, to hire a hitman to carry out Mr. Pannun’s murder for a total sum of $100,000. Mr. Yadav, who was arrested in December 2023 in Delhi in a separate case of kidnapping and extortion, has been out on bail since April 2024.

fullParagraphs: Billionaire Deepinder Goyal has begun selling Temple, a temple-attached wearable he says can monitor brain health and ageing by measuring cerebral blood flow outside the lab. Critics and doctors question the device’s medical claims, noting the evidence is preliminary, not peer-reviewed, and its core metric—the Brain Flow index—remains controversial amid concerns over links to longevity or cognitive outcomes

Billionaire entrepreneur Deepinder Goyal, co-founder of Zomato and Blinkit, has announced the commercial availability of Temple, a wearable monitoring device that he claims could become “Humanity’s last personal device”.

A graduate in Computer Science and Mathematics from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, Mr. Goyal has no academic background in medical sciences or biological research. His claims have drawn criticism from doctors, including social media influencer and physician Cyriac Abby Philips (LiverDoc), who has described the device as a “scam”.

While Deepavali marks the culmination of the festive celebrations for many communities across India, people from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and parts of West Bengal are preparing for another important festival — Chhath Puja . Ahead of the celebrations, the Telangana government has directed civic bodies and disaster management authorities to facilitate Chhath Puja at 28 locations across the city and make necessary arrangements, including sanitation, lighting, drinking water and crowd management. In a recent memo, the Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MAUD) department has forwarded the association’s representation to the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), and the three municipal corporations asking them to take necessary action in coordination with the departments concerned.

Chhath Puja is dedicated to the worship of the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya. The Sun is worshipped as the source of life, energy and sustenance. Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun, seeking good health, prosperity, happiness and the well-being of their families.
Devotees offer prayers to the setting and rising Sun during Chhath Puja festival. File | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Chhath Puja is a four-day festival, with each day having a distinct ritual. The first day, Nahay Khay, involves devotees taking a ritual bath, cleaning their homes and preparing a traditional meal. The second day, Kharna, involves a day-long fast, which is broken after sunset with offerings such as jaggery-based kheer, chapati and fruits. Following this, devotees undertake a rigorous fast without food and water.

On the third day, known as Sandhya Arghya, devotees gather at rivers, lakes, ponds and other water bodies to offer prayers to the setting Sun. Standing in water, they make offerings of fruits, sugarcane and traditional preparations. The festival concludes on the fourth day with Usha Arghya, when devotees return to the water bodies before sunrise to offer prayers to the rising Sun. The rituals conclude with devotees breaking their fast.

The proposed locations fall under the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) and Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation (MMC) limits. Some of the proposed locations include Tank Bund, Hasmatpet Lake, Durgam Cheruvu, Shamirpet, Miyapur and Uppal, among several others.

The association has proposed celebrations at 28 specifically named locations, apart from other Bathukamma ghats in and around the city. The Bihar Association has urged the civic bodies to clean and maintain the designated ghats and surrounding areas, with particular attention to sanitation and hygiene. It has also sought adequate lighting at the ghats and approach roads, drinking water facilities and other essential public amenities. With devotees expected to gather for the evening prayers on November 15 and the morning rituals on November 16, the association has specifically requested adequate lighting during these periods.

Other requests include crowd management and traffic regulation in coordination with the Police Department, provision of chairs, carpets and mats, public-address systems and, wherever necessary, stages or platforms to facilitate the organised conduct of the celebrations. The association has also sought necessary safety and civic arrangements to ensure that devotees can perform the rituals in a safe, clean and orderly environment.

articles.title: Andhra government expected to make significant allocations for Neradi barrage to be constructed on Vamsadhara river
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to BRR Vamsadhara Project Chairman Aravala Ravindrababu, the State government which had given an administrative sanction for ₹461 crores a couple of months back, may give additional sanctions in the next budget

The Andhra Pradesh government is expected to make allocations in the next annual budget of the State for the year 2027-28 for the construction of Neradi barrage across Vamsadhara River and ensure dedicated water facility for nearly 2.56 lakh acres of lands in Srikakulam district of AP, which has waited nearly 55 years to overcome water dispute with the neighbouring Odisha State.

According to BRR Vamsadhara Project Chairman Aravala Ravindrababu, the State government which had given an administrative sanction for ₹461 crores a couple of months back, may give additional sanctions in the next budget. “On the request from Union Minister for Civil Aviation K. Rammohan Naidu, the Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is keen to complete Neradi barrage within a couple of years. As a first step, it has given administrative sanction to ensure compensation for land acquisition and other needs,” said Mr. Ravindrababu while speaking to The Hindu .

Six days ago, the AP government proposed this project for optimum utilisation of water of Vamsadhara which flows nearly 82 km across Srikakulam district after flowing across 154 km in Odisha from its origin in Kalahandi district of neighbouring State. However, it was not taken up as 106 acres of land in Odisha had to be acquired for this project.

Vamsadhara Water Disputes Tribunal, which was appointed to oversee the issue, has asked AP to pay compensation for the land in Odisha and construct the project. Although the order was given in the year 2021, the Union Ministry of Water Resources has not given its nod for the project till the intervention of Mr. Chandrababu Naidu and Mr. Rammohan Naidu. As the Centre had given a notification recently, AP is all set to take up the project which might need around ₹1,099 crores. The initial allocation of ₹461 crore would ensure completion of land acquisition and beginning of the works. Mr. Ravindrababu said that the project would help farmers to grow three crops in a year in several mandals including Bhamini, Amudalavalasa, Srikakulam, Narasannapeta and others.

articles.title: Explosions heard in Saudi capital Riyadh: AFP journalists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: AFP journalists heard the blasts, and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an aerial threat

Multiple explosions were heard in the Saudi capital on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), as the military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh.
AFP journalists heard the blasts and residents received an alert on their mobile phones instructing them to take shelter due to an "aerial threat".
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," the Saudi-led coalition posted on X.
A subsequent message from the country's civil defence agency said the danger had passed.
The coalition had earlier said air defences also destroyed a ballistic missile headed towards the southern region overnight.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil exporter, has faced near-daily strikes from the Houthis for weeks, after a truce in their long-running conflict unravelled in July.
On Sunday (November 8), the Houthis claimed attacks on Riyadh's business district, where witnesses said the Aramco Tower was damaged.
Saudi authorities said the building suffered minor damage from falling shrapnel after an "attempted attack".

Images released by Saudi Arabia's press agency on Tuesday (November 10) showed the Riyadh region's deputy governor and other officials inspecting the building, with visible damage to some of its floors.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Aramco tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company's headquarters.
The coalition has in response been launching airstrikes against Houthi positions inside Yemen.

According to Houthi news agency Saba, Saudi warplanes on Tuesday (November 10) carried out a series of strikes on the capital Sanaa and its outskirts, targeting a gas facility and a building belonging to the Yemeni state oil company.

articles.title: What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them

There is a major shift happening in Capitol Hill following the U.S. midterm elections, as Representative Thomas Massie supported by lawmakers, including Representative Ro Khanna, introduced eight Articles of impeachment against U.S. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth.
The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.

Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him.
Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution.
Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026.

The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S.

Article II focuses on Mr. Hegseth’s refusal to comply with Congress’s directive to withdraw U.S. forces from Iran. After both the House and Senate passed House Concurrent Resolution 86 (the first successful passage of such a legislative vehicle by both chambers of Congress in the history of the United States of America) to end unauthorised hostilities in June 2026, Mr. Hegseth allegedly directed the Department of Defence to ignore the resolution and continue with military strikes.

As per Section 5 (b) of the War Powers Resolution, authorised military action must terminate within 60 days (after a report is submitted or is required to be submitted to Congress). Article III alleges Mr. Hegseth continued conducting hostile military operations in Iran beyond the mandatory statutory deadlines of May 1 and June 1, 2026, without congressional extensions.

This Article accuses Mr. Hegseth of “cultivating a warmaking culture” and a “course of conduct that effected the systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defence infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians and non-military objects during military operations”, among other allegations.
It specifically highlights the February 28, 2026, cruise missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Iran, which killed and wounded over 200 civilians, mostly children.

Article V targets a strike campaign against suspected narcotics smuggling vessels in international waters (in the Caribbean Sea and Eastern Pacific Ocean) that resulted in at least 221 deaths across 63 attack events.

It charges Mr. Hegseth with using lethal military force instead of standard maritime law enforcement framework (sections 102 and 522 of Title 14), lowering targeting standards, and ordering or permitting actions that denied quarter and failed to rescue shipwrecked survivors.

The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela.

Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him.

Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution.

Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026.

The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S.

Article II focuses on Mr. Hegseth’s refusal to comply with Congress’s directive to withdraw U.S. forces from Iran. After both the House and Senate passed House Concurrent Resolution 86 (the first successful passage of such a legislative vehicle by both chambers of Congress in the history of the United States of America) to end unauthorised hostilities in June 2026, Mr. Hegseth allegedly directed the Department of Defence to ignore the resolution and continue with military strikes.

As per Section 5 (b) of the War Powers Resolution, authorised military action must terminate within 60 days (after a report is submitted or is required to be submitted to Congress). Article III alleges Mr. Hegseth continued conducting hostile military operations in Iran beyond the mandatory statutory deadlines of May 1 and June 1, 2026, without congressional extensions.

This Article accuses Mr. Hegseth of “cultivating a warmaking culture” and a “course of conduct that effected the systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defence infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians and non-military objects during military operations”, among other allegations.

It specifically highlights the February 28, 2026, cruise missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Iran, which killed and wounded over 200 civilians, mostly children.

Article V targets a strike campaign against suspected narcotics smuggling vessels in international waters (in the Caribbean Sea and Eastern Pacific Ocean) that resulted in at least 221 deaths across 63 attack events.

It charges Mr. Hegseth with using lethal military force instead of standard maritime law enforcement framework (sections 102 and 522 of Title 14), lowering targeting standards, and ordering or permitting actions that denied quarter and failed to rescue shipwrecked survivors.

articles.title: Republican Thomas Massie of Kentucky launches bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Thomas Massie, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Pete Hegseth's actions amounted to high crimes and misdemeanors

Rep Thomas Massie on Monday (November 9, 2026) moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing his fellow Republicans to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses blamed in part on fallout from the war in Iran.

Mr. Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the impeachment resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth's role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela.
The Congressman, who was defeated by a Trump-backed challenger in a primary earlier this year, said Mr. Hegseth's actions amounted to “high crimes and misdemeanors.”
Mr. Hegseth, he said, “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.”
President Donald Trump lashed out at Massie personally just hours after the Congressman read the resolution, calling him a “loser” who “has a lot of hatred in his heart.”

A vote in the House could come by mid-week, but next steps are highly uncertain. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries supports the measure. If most Democrats follow him, Mr. Massie would only need support from a few Republicans to impeach Hegseth.

If the House votes to impeach, it would fall to to the Senate to either dismiss the charges or hold a trial. Republicans remain in the majority in both chambers, until the new Congress convenes in January with Democrats in control.
Sen Chuck Schumer, the Democratic leader, endorsed the impeachment push. "Hegseth must stand trial before the Senate," he said.

Republican leaders, who are eager to use their final weeks in power executing their own agenda, expressed frustration at the move. House Speaker Mike Johnson, who has tried to prevent the vote, said impeachment “in the middle of hostilities abroad would be a terrible, terrible look, a terrible thing for our allies and our enemies to see that.”
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he wasn't sure why the vote was being held now.
“We'll see what their ultimate decision is over there,” he said of the House. “We'll have to deal with it accordingly here."

Mr. Hegseth is stepping up his public statements ahead of the vote, telling reporters that he's eager to defend the military actions that he and Mr. Trump have taken against Iran, Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Venezuela's previous leaders.

articles.title: What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.
Map showing the alleged locations of Megaspeed International | Photo Credit: Screengrab from LinkedIn

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

As per an AFP report, in 2025, Bloomberg News also reported on the Singaporean probe into Megaspeed over the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China. According to AFP , Megaspeed retorted in December of the same year, saying that Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

Jensen Huang, the top boss of the chip maker and one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, has admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship with Alice Huang. The Nvidia CEO said that he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife, my actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” the statement, uploaded on Nvidia’s website added.
The New York Times reported that Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang.

articles.title: Anthropic sends out, then retracts details of IPO filing, emails show
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Anthropic ‌sent out and ​then ⁠retracted details of its blockbuster IPO filing, ‌according to emails to bankers

Details of Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO, ​including plans by the AI company to raise nearly $70 billion, were briefly ⁠circulated to banks before being retracted late on Monday, according to emails seen by Reuters.

A representative of Anthropic sent a copy of a securities filing that showed it aimed to sell about 867 ‌million shares at a price range of $70 to $80 per share, then followed up with an email saying details about the pricing were inaccurate. Anthropic said in ‌the second email it would update the filing later.
Anthropic declined to comment. The email ‌did ⁠not specify to bankers what was erroneous, and Reuters was unable to ⁠determine what was incorrect.

The original email whose details were retracted showed Anthropic planned to sell 866.7 million Class A shares, including a secondary offering. Anthropic itself would sell about 843.3 million shares, while existing shareholders would sell an additional ​23.3 million shares. The IPO would ‌raise $69.3 billion at the top of the range.

Separately, the original filing showed that Anthropic had lined up $26 billion in investments from some of the world’s biggest technology companies alongside its IPO, underscoring the increasingly intertwined financial ties underpinning the AI boom.

Alphabet’s Google, Nvidia, ‌Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, Microsoft and TSMC had agreed to participate in the ​private placement of Anthropic’s Class N common stock at the IPO price, which would close immediately after the IPO, the original filing showed.
Anthropic is ⁠expected to formally launch the roadshow on Tuesday, with pricing expected in the following week.

The Anthropic IPO comes at a time when other companies in the AI infrastructure and data center ‌sectors have delayed or withdrawn their planned listings, facing a rise in interest rates that has helped fuel a punishing selloff in shares and bonds of AI operators such as CoreWeave Inc and broader questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

Investors had previously discussed a valuation of as much as $2 trillion for Anthropic, but expectations have since come down, with the $1.5 trillion figure viewed as the high end of the range, Reuters previously reported.

Founded in ‌2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic’s president, Anthropic ​has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models.

The company’s rapid growth has been underpinned by Google and ⁠Amazon, which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as ⁠AI competitors.

Anthropic had nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, underscoring how its rapid growth depends on vast amounts of future capacity, some ‌of it reliant on financing beyond the company’s control.

articles.title: 331 tonnes of garbage removed from Madurai city after Deepavali
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Madurai Corporation cleared a total of 331 tonnes of garbage, till 6 p.m. on Monday, which was generated across the city on Deepavali day.
Along with the corporation cleanliness workers, volunteers from the Democratic Youth Federation of India, joined the mass cleaning drive early on Monday morning.
Mayor (in-charge), T. Nagarajan, and Corporation Commissioner, Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated the cleanliness drive.

The drive started on the Chithrai Streets, Aavani Moola Streets, Masi Streets, Veli Streets and Vilakkuthoon junction around Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple where commercial establishments, especially textile showrooms, are located.
Besides, the workers focussed on spots at Teppakulam, Mattuthavani bus stand and Vaigai Bank Roads where garbage accumulation is higher.
Besides the usual vehicles used for transporting garbage, 11 earth movers, five bobcat machinery, nine tipper trucks and 42 tractors were involved in the exercise.

The work was expedited in the early hours so much so that 128.40 tonnes of garbage was cleared in the city by 12 noon. This was 33.32 tonnes of additional festival-time garbage removed when compared to 95.08 tonnes cleared during the same time in the last Deepavali season.
The workers had already removed 137 tonnes of garbage on Deepavali day (Sunday).
City Health Officer, Aravind Jothi, Assistant Health Officer, Abishek, DYFI district president, Selva, and secretary, Vel Deva, were present.

articles.title: FDA adds rare vision-loss warning to popular obesity, diabetes drugs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss and has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs,

Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, U.S. health regulators announced Monday, November 9, 2026.

The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labelling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.

The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn't understood, the FDA said.
FDA scientists began looking into the problem after the publication of a 2024 medical paper tying the condition to certain patients taking semaglutide, the active drug in Eli Lilly's Ozempic.

An FDA analysis of more than 125 clinical trials found that the problem occurred in roughly 6 of every 100,000 patients who took a GLP-1 for at least one year. The comparable rate for people taking a placebo or other types of glucose-lowering medications was less than 4 per 100,000, the FDA said.
The agency also found reports of the problem in its electronic reporting system for drug injuries and side effects.

Symptoms of the problem include blurred vision, blind spots, distorted colors and other visual disturbances, according to the FDA. Patients experiencing such problems should contact a health care professional immediately, the agency said.

articles.title: Andhra Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan to part ways with wife, Anna Lezhneva
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a joint statement, the couple said that, after sharing a significant part of their lives together, they had decided to separate
Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan and his wife Anna Lezhneva have decided to part ways “with mutual understanding and respect”.
In a joint statement shared with the media on Monday night (November 9, 2026), the couple said that, after sharing a significant part of their lives together, they had decided to separate.
“Though our marriage has come to an end, we remain good friends and devoted parents to our wonderful children. Their happiness and wellbeing will always remain our shared priority,” they said.
Mr. Kalyan and Ms. Lezhneva said they were seeking understanding, kindness and respect for their privacy during this personal transition.
They added that they were extending heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has stood by them throughout their journey.

Mr. Kalyan and Ms. Lezhneva married in September 2013. She is Russian and reportedly worked as a model and an actor. The couple has one daughter, Polena Anjana Pawanova, and one son, Mark Shankar Pawanovich.

articles.title: Award-winning Keralam farmer who used his banana farming as cover for smuggling drugs arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dhanesh S. Nair had allegedly trained members of his drug network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches
The Ernakulam Rural police have arrested an award-winning 31-year-old farmer suspected to be running a drug network under the cover of his agriculture ventures.

Dhanesh S. Nair, aka Dani, of Haripad, Alappuzha district was arrested with 803 grams of suspected hashish oil and 8 grams of suspected MDMA, the police said on Monday (November 9, 2026). The investigating team zeroed in on the accused as part of the probe into the recent arrest of Harikrishnan K.S., 32, of Palluruthy, Kochi with 185 gram of suspected MDMA from a lodge in Aluva.

The accused, who lives near Nanjanagudu, Mysuru, was nabbed by a special investigation team, led by District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan when he landed in Angamaly. The police suspect he was engaged in drug peddling under the cover of banana cultivation in Nanjanagudu.

He had reportedly pursued a higher education programme in Agribusiness in Germany between 2015 and 2018. He later returned to Keralam during the floods in 2018 and ventured into farming. The police said he had won a government award for the best young farmer in Haripad in 2022.

He had allegedly trained members of his network on how to conceal drugs inside banana bunches. Videos of the accused showing them methods to conceal drugs inside banana bunches were allegedly recovered from his mobile phone. The banana bunches were transported to Keralam under the guise of carrying agricultural produce. He had reportedly recruited youth to transport and distribute the drugs in Bengaluru and nearby areas. The drugs were later brought to Keralam and distributed among local suppliers and consumers.

Earlier, the police had held Shinu Sebastian, 34, of Thoppumpady with seven gram of suspected MDMA following the arrest of Mr. Harikrishnan. The police, sources said, suspect Mr. Harikrishnan and Mr. Sebastian were engaged in alleged drug peddling as per instructions given by Mr. Nair through social media.

articles.title: Supreme Court goes beyond Deepavali AQI, flags vehicular emissions polluting Delhi air
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court says Delhi and the NCR bear the ‘cumulative burden of vehicular traffic’ and seeks to know what has been done to regulate in the capital the entry and plying of vehicles from neighbouring States

Forty-eight hours before Deepavali, amidst the rising crescendo of crackers heralding the festivities, a Supreme Court Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the people, and not the judiciary, must strike a blow against air pollution in the national capital.

Instead, the court went beyond Deepavali to highlight a consistent danger that sustains and would worsen the toxic air: vehicular emissions. On November 6, the court detected a sharp increase in issues attributable to vehicular emissions.

It told the authorities that the thick smog, which later raised the city’s Air Quality Index (AQI) to almost the ‘severe’ category following Deepavali, had nowhere to go in the landlocked capital. The substantial commercial and non-commercial traffic entering Delhi would only compound the problem in the coming days.

“It must be borne in mind that Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), by virtue of their geographical and economic interconnectedness, bear the cumulative burden of vehicular traffic originating not merely within their own boundaries but also from the neighbouring States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan,” the Supreme Court reminded the authorities in its latest order.

The issue warranted urgent and immediate intervention, the court said, directing the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), the Delhi government, the Delhi Police (Traffic department), as well as the neighbouring States of Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh to file their responses on what they have done to regulate in the national capital the entry and plying of commercial and non-commercial vehicles.

The court wanted to know about measures to regulate traffic originating from outside the national capital. These include steps taken to identify, monitor, and regulate vehicles that do not conform to prescribed emission standards, and measures to prevent the entry and operation of overage, end-of-life, or non-compliant vehicles.

The Bench has specifically sought information on the measures undertaken against violations, including the number of vehicles inspected, challaned, denied entry, and the coordination mechanisms between the authorities of Delhi and the neighbouring States for regulating inter-State vehicular movement.

The court has asked if the authorities have any “further short-term and long-term measures proposed or contemplated to mitigate vehicular emissions and reduce their contribution to the deteriorating air quality in Delhi and the National Capital Region”.

Incidentally, two separate orders of the Supreme Court passed several months ago, on January 21 and February 23 this year, had contained detailed long-term and short-term measures recommended by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to mitigate air pollution, especially caused by vehicular emissions, in Delhi.

The January 21 order had listed various CAQM recommendations, including phasing out polluting vehicles from Delhi-NCR, fortifying the pollution-under-check regime, augmentation of rail transport and metro models, revised electric vehicle policy, among others.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, for CAQM, had, at the time, submitted that a meta-analysis of studies from 2015 to 2025 attributed PM2.5 in Delhi to a mix of primary emissions and secondary particulate formation from sources within the national capital region itself. The measures suggested by the CAQM included developing multi-modal transport hubs connecting the metro, Regional Rapid Transit System, and last-mile connectivity with a real-time passenger information system, higher incentives to owners for scrapping old vehicles, expansion in EV charging infrastructure, etc.

“We direct the concerned agencies, particularly, the MCD, to submit their immediate response as to why these measures be not implemented without any delay. Once again, we clarify that no objections will be entertained against the recommendations made by the CAQM,” the court had made its intent clear on January 21.

articles.title: Keralam CPI(M) awaits ICC report on complaint against former Palakkad secretary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Complainant had made allegations of sexual misconduct against Babu; party State leadership to decide on further action based on findings in report

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] has stepped up its internal inquiry into a sexual misconduct complaint against former Palakkad district secretary E.N. Suresh Babu. The party’s internal complaints committee (ICC) is investigating the complaint. It has reportedly completed key procedures, including recording the statement of the woman who filed the complaint.
The complainant is a lawyer and a party leader. She is understood to have submitted digital evidence in support of her allegations against Mr. Babu.

The ICC will submit its inquiry report and recommendations to the CPI(M) State committee after completing the investigation. The State leadership will decide on further action against Mr. Babu based on the findings. The possibility of disciplinary action, including removal from primary membership, is also being discussed within the party.

As per the party’s rules, a complaint against a leader of an organisational unit must be investigated by the ICC of the next higher committee. Since Mr. Babu was the Palakkad district secretary when the complaint was raised, the matter was referred to the ICC under the party central committee.

The woman’s complaint had earlier led to the intervention of the State leadership and Mr. Babu’s removal from the district secretary post. On October 4, the party appointed former MLA V. Chenthamarakshan as his successor at an extended district committee meeting. The CPI(M) had officially described the change as part of its organisational review following the electoral setback.

The party had maintained that Mr. Babu stepped down voluntarily due to personal reasons, denying any link between his removal and the complaint. However, the ICC inquiry has brought the circumstances surrounding his exit as district secretary back into focus.
The complaint reportedly relates to an incident at the CPI(M) district committee office in Palakkad, where the woman had been called.

The issue is likely to come up for further discussion at the State leadership level after the ICC submits its report. The findings and recommendations will determine the next course of action against Mr. Babu.

articles.title: Oxford University returns remains of 39 Naga people after more than a century
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on November 9, 2026
The University of Oxford returned the remains of 39 members of the Naga community, which were held at its Pitt Rivers Museum for more than a century, in a historic repatriation initiative.
The remains were formally handed over to the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) and the Naga Tribe Hoho at a ceremony held at the museum on Monday (November 9, 2026).

The transfer of title document was signed by Pitt Rivers Museum Director Professor Laura Van Broekhoven and FNR representative Rev. Dr. Wati Aier. It was witnessed by Visier Sanyu on behalf of the FNR and Thejao Vihienuo representing the Naga Tribe Hoho.
Following the handover, the ancestral remains were moved from the University of Oxford to begin their journey to Nagaland, according to a statement issued by the FNR on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

The remains had been part of the collections of the Pitt Rivers Museum, established in 1884, which houses cultural artefacts collected from various parts of the world. Addressing the ceremony, University of Oxford Vice-Chancellor Professor Irene Tracey described the handover as a historic moment in the relationship between the university and the Naga people.
“She said the initiative reflected a community-led effort towards reconciliation, healing and peace,” the statement said.

Mr. Sanyu spoke about the impact of British colonial violence on Naga communities and recounted how his own village was burnt by colonial forces. Emphasising the importance of forgiveness and reconciliation, he quoted late Naga peace activist Niketu Iralu as saying, "Hate not transformed is transferred".

Thejao Vihienuo, president of the Angami Public Organisation, who represented the Naga Tribe Hoho, said the return of the ancestral remains was the right of the Naga people to care for their ancestors. He called for the return of all Naga ancestral remains held in museums to their homeland with dignity.
Meanwhile, preparations have begun for the burial of the remains at Naga Solidarity Park in Kohima. The Naga Solidarity Park Management Committee has allocated a designated site within the park.
A prayer service was recently held at the park to mark the formal commencement of preparatory work for the proposed burial site, the committee's convenor Vipopal Kintsi said.
“The proposed burial is intended to provide a common resting place for the ancestral remains and promote healing, reconciliation and unity among the Naga people,” he said.
Mr. Kintsi said the homecoming of the remains should transcend historical and tribal divisions and strengthen a shared sense of Naga identity.

articles.title: Former DMK Minister Anbil Mahesh’s bail plea dismissed in alleged multi-crore private school bribery case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Anbil Mahesh was arrested on October 26 and remanded in judicial custody till November 18

A special court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) dismissed the bail petition filed by former Tamil Nadu School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, who is accused of receiving a share of an alleged multi-crore bribe collected from private school managements allegedly through threats, deception, and false promises of securing government approvals.

D.C. Elangovan, secretary of the Private School Management Association, lodged a complaint with the Chennai Commissioner of Police on June 23, 2026, alleging that nearly ₹100 crore had been collected from private school managements through intimidation and forgery.

The complaint named B.T. Arasakumar (Accused 1), who allegedly floated an unregistered body called the Tamil Nadu Private Schools Association (TNPSA), claiming to be its founder-president, and Muthukumar (Accused 2), a former MLA from Virudhachalam, as the key persons involved in the collection of bribes.

The two allegedly organised an event of the TNPSA at Kalaivanar Arangam in Chennai on December 30, 2024, which Mr. Poyyamozhi attended as the chief guest. The prosecution alleged that a bank account was subsequently opened in the name of BTK Educational Development Trust at the Canara Bank’s Tondiarpet branch; this account was used to collect membership fees and other amounts from private schools.

The FIR alleged that the accused assured school managements that they could obtain government approvals and permissions easily, even if their institutions lacked basic requirements. They allegedly threatened that schools refusing to pay the demanded amounts would not receive the necessary permissions, potentially affecting students appearing for the SSLC and Class XII public examinations.

Dismissing the bail petition, Special Court Judge L.S. Sathiyamurthy noted that statements from witnesses, including private school correspondents and managers, had been recorded by the investigating officer and before the Judicial Magistrate. “A preliminary examination of these statements indicated a prima facie link between the petitioner and the alleged offence,” the judge observed.

The investigating agency had also seized computers and other digital devices from Mr. Poyyamozhi’s premises and sent them to a forensic laboratory for examination. The court said it would have to await the findings of the cyber forensic experts.

Observing that the investigation was still at an early stage and the first period of remand had only just concluded, the Special Court Judge said the materials collected so far indicated that substantial sums had been extorted from multiple private school managements through deception and threats. Witness statements suggested that money collected by A1, A2, and their associates had reached the petitioner under the guise of a ‘party fund’, it said.

Classifying the case as a multi-crore economic offence involving several victims, the court pointed out that some of the accused were yet to be arrested and the custodial interrogation of Muthukumar who had surrendered after the arrest of Mr. Poyyamozhi and other accused, was at an initial stage.

The court also underscored the responsibility attached to public office, observing that the petitioner, as School Education Minister, had been entrusted with the welfare of students, teachers, and parents.

Holding that public interest, particularly the welfare and education of schoolchildren, outweighed the petitioner’s (Mr. Poyyamozhi) claim for bail at this stage, Mr. Sathiyamurthy dismissed the petition.
