The investigating agency had also seized computers and other digital devices from Mr. Poyyamozhi’s premises and sent them to a forensic laboratory for examination. The court said it would have to await the findings of the cyber forensic experts.

Observing that the investigation was still at an early stage and the first period of remand had only just concluded, the Special Court Judge said the materials collected so far indicated that substantial sums had been extorted from multiple private school managements through deception and threats. Witness statements suggested that money collected by A1, A2, and their associates had reached the petitioner under the guise of a ‘party fund’, it said.

Classifying the case as a multi-crore economic offence involving several victims, the court pointed out that some of the accused were yet to be arrested and the custodial interrogation of Muthukumar who had surrendered after the arrest of Mr. Poyyamozhi and other accused, was at an initial stage.

The court also underscored the responsibility attached to public office, observing that the petitioner, as School Education Minister, had been entrusted with the welfare of students, teachers, and parents.

Holding that public interest, particularly the welfare and education of schoolchildren, outweighed the petitioner’s (Mr. Poyyamozhi) claim for bail at this stage, Mr. Sathiyamurthy dismissed the petition.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process
Several industry bodies have urged the Ministry of Finance to rationalise long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equities and reduce securities transaction tax (STT) in the upcoming Union Budget 2027.

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been holding pre-Budget consultative meetings with the main industry bodies such as the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), and the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI).

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was to rationalise LTCG tax on equities, particularly in view of the tax concessions extended to certain debt instruments. However, several other tax proposals related to the capital market also feature in the recommendations.

The PHDCCI, for example, has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about ₹3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

Budget 2027 will be presented against the backdrop of the ongoing West Asia crisis, rising inflation, and fiscal pressure on the government. In this, India’s micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) need help, the industry bodies have argued.

Towards this, PHDCCI has requested the Finance Minister to extend the overdue period for classifying a loan as a non-performing asset (NPA) from the existing 90 days to 180 days. The move, it argued, would “accommodate longer working capital cycles and delayed realisation of receivables”.

Further, the chamber has called for an enhancement of PM MUDRA loan limits and a Budget announcement of direct equity support to MSMEs through the Fund of Funds Scheme, “with dedicated allocations for start-up seed capital and SME IPO participation.

articles.title: Malaysian court clears final hurdle for former PM Najib Razak's transfer to house arrest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “A High Court in Malaysia on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) cleared all legal hurdles for the transfer of imprisoned former Prime Minister Najib Razak to his home to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest,” his lawyer said.
Najib has been behind bars since August 2022, when the Kuala Lumpur High Court upheld his graft conviction linked to a multibillion-dollar looting of the state investment fund 1MDB.
In September, Najib was granted royal clemency, allowing him to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest once he pays a court-imposed fine.

Last Friday, he left prison after his political party paid the 50 million ringgit ($12.3 million) fine but he was brought back hours later after the attorney general blocked the transfer, seeking legal clarifications.

The attorney general's request sparked a public rebuke from the palace, which said that King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar's prerogative of pardon for Najib that allowed the house arrest was clear and must be respected. It said any attempts to challenge it would amount to defying the royal order.

Najib's lawyer Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said on Tuesday all was settled for the former Prime Minister's transfer to house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur home, where he is to remain until Aug 23, 2028. Najib appeared in court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026); the transfer was expected to take place later in the day. Police later sealed off the road leading to his home. “It's a final relief, you know, great sigh to him because he has been waiting for this,” the lawyer said.

The house arrest covers only Najib's reduced, six-year sentence in his first trial for graft and not a separate, 15-year sentence handed down last December for corruption and money laundering. That sentence followed a second major trial tied to the 1MDB scandal.
Najib is also appealing that sentence, which he is to serve after the end of his first sentence. If his appeal fails, he could return to prison after his house arrest ends.

Najib, who served as Prime Minister from 2009 to 2018, has denied any wrongdoing. He is Malaysia's first former leader to be imprisoned under a sentence related to the 1MDB scandal. It marked one of the world's largest financial scandals, rippling across global markets and triggering investigations in the United States and other countries.

articles.title: Bangladesh prosecutor says ex-PM Hasina will be executed if she returns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict,’ Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.
The Bangladeshi prosecutor who secured the death sentence against ousted leader Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) she will be executed if she returns home.

Ms. Hasina, whose 15-year rule was ended by a mass uprising she tried to crush, has vowed to return in December to Bangladesh, where she was convicted of crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters.
"Sheikh Hasina has no option but to face the execution of the verdict," Md Aminul Islam told reporters, responding to reports she planned to return from self-imposed exile in neighbouring India.
He added that the 79-year-old fugitive had missed the deadline to appeal against her conviction, leaving her with no further legal recourse.
"The statutory appeal period has expired, and no appeal can now be filed," he said.

The daughter of a revolutionary who led Bangladesh to independence in 1971, Ms. Hasina presided over breakneck economic growth, helping transform the South Asian nation of 170 million people from a largely agricultural economy into a global manufacturing hub.
Critics have accused Ms. Hasina of jailing political rivals, enacting harsh anti-press laws and overseeing widespread human rights abuses, including the killing of opposition activists.
Her 2024 crackdown left up to 1,400 people dead, according to the United Nations.
She fled to neighbouring India by helicopter in August 2024 as angry crowds stormed her palace.
She has remained there ever since, hidden from public view. Only occasionally has she addressed news conferences by telephone, her voice sounding frail.
Ms. Hasina has repeatedly said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December, telling AFP she is "fully aware" she faces being hanged if she returns.
She said "fear cannot decide" her "duty to the people".

articles.title: Poland arrests two Ukrainians over alleged Russian espionage, sabotage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Poland has arrested two Ukrainian men suspected of espionage ​and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence ‌services, the Internal Security Agency (ABW) ​said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

Poland has long ⁠accused Russia and its ally Belarus of waging a hybrid campaign involving sabotage, cyberattacks ‌and disinformation since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Russia has repeatedly ‌denied the accusations.

“According to findings ‌by ⁠the ABW, the suspects carried ⁠out tasks on behalf of Russian special services, which included, among other things, reconnoitring critical infrastructure ​and military facilities ‌throughout the country,” the agency said in a statement.

“The prosecutor has charged both detainees with engaging in espionage activities ‌on behalf of a foreign ​intelligence service against the Republic of Poland, as well as ⁠committing acts of sabotage.”

According to investigators, the men set fire to vehicles after replacing ‌their licence plates with ones resembling those used by the Ukrainian military. The men were paid for carrying out the tasks, including in cryptocurrencies.

“The investigation has established that the ‌acts of sabotage were carried out at the ​behest of Russian intelligence services and were intended to fuel anti-Ukrainian ⁠sentiment,” prosecutors said in a separate statement.
Both ⁠face from 10 years to life imprisonment if found guilty.
The Russian ‌embassy in Warsaw did not immediately respond to an emailed request ​for comment.

articles.title: Kadambini Ganguly: breaking barriers in medicine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: In her time, Kadambini Ganguly challenged convention to become the first Indian female doctor to practice Western medicine

Have you heard of the names Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi? Considered India’s first female doctors, these names have often been looked past in the pages of history and even medical textbooks. Today, let’s talk about the story of Kadambini Ganguly — India’s first practising lady doctor.

It was in 1861 that Brahmo reformer and headmaster Braja Kishore Basu had a daughter. She was named Kadambini Basu. Young Kadambini, despite hailing from a community that did not necessarily support women’s education like many others at the time did, received an education at the Brahmo Eden Female School and later at the Hindu Mahila Vidyalaya.

As the daughter of someone who organised and fought for women’s emancipation, Kadambini went on to study in college and became the first woman to pass the University of Calcutta entrance examination. In 1882, she passed the examination for the Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree along with Chandramukhi Basu from the University of Calcutta, making her and Chandramukhi the first female graduates in the country.

Wanting to study medicine, Kadambini decided to enrol at the Calcutta Medical College after graduation. She was, however, believed to have been unable to receive the BMC certificate due to a shortage of a couple of marks. She did receive the GBMC (Graduate of Bengal Medical College) degree, though, in 1886. Thus, she became the first Indian woman to be allowed to practice Western medicine.

Around 1888, Kadambini started working at the Lady Dufferin Hospital for a monthly salary of 300 rupees. She had even gone to Nepal to treat British royalty. Along with pursuing medicine, she was also politically quite vocal and active. Around 1899, Kadambini was one of the first women delegates elected to the Fifth Session of the Congress in Bombay and the next year, she won to become the first women speaker at the Congress.

She also served as the president of the Transvaal Indian Association, founded by Gandhiji’s colleague Henry Pollock. She was a member of the Women’s Conference held in Calcutta and even presided over the General Brahmo Samaj session in Calcutta.

Around 1883, Kadambini married Dwarakanath Ganguly (thus the change in name from Kadambini Bose to Kadambini Ganguly in many documents). Dwarakanath Ganguly was a Bengali Brahmo reformer, educator, journalist, and pioneer of women’s rights in British India.

She was a mother to eight children and is often said to have been deft in needlework. She became a practising doctor while equally devoting herself to family and household affairs, an action which was deemed impossible by many in the era.

Despite having being burdened with domestic chores, like most women of that time, Kadambini still managed to smash the glass ceilings and societal stereotypes in both her professional and personal life.
A name which should not be forgotten in the course of time, Dr Kadambini is a reason many of us are able to pursue our passion — in medicine and in life.

articles.title: BJP sets sights on grassroots expansion ahead of A.P. panchayat polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: State president P.V.N. Madhav urges leaders to secure a presence in every village and panchayat, building on the party’s gains in municipal corporations, ZPTCs and MPTCs

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has identified the forthcoming panchayat elections as an opportunity to strengthen its presence across Andhra Pradesh, with State president P.V.N. Madhav urging party leaders to ensure representation in every village and panchayat.

Addressing a State-level workshop on local body election results, Mr. Madhav said the BJP had secured representation in all 13 municipal corporations that went to polls in the first phase. It had won about 23 of the 33 ZPTC seats contested and secured MPTC seats. Around 355 party representatives had been elected across the State, he said.

The three-phase panchayat elections, scheduled for November 13, 17 and 19, were crucial to expanding the party at the grassroots. He called for stronger coordination among alliance partners and effective utilisation of Central funds released to panchayats.

BJP national vice-president and Rajamahendravaram MP Daggubati Purandeswari attributed the party’s electoral gains to the efforts of generations of workers. The BJP had won more than 59% of the seats allotted to it under the alliance arrangement, she said.
Citing its performance in the erstwhile combined East Godavari district, she said the party had won 10 of 11 seats in Anaparthi, all three in Gopalapuram and both seats allotted to it in Kovvur.
She urged elected representatives to remain accessible to party workers and called for grooming a new generation of leaders to take the organisation forward over the next 10 to 15 years.

articles.title: Mannarkkad gears up to host Kerala State school science fair from November 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 7,000 students expected to take part in event; Minister Samsudheen chairs review meeting to assess preparations made by various committees, subcommittees
The 58th State school science fair will be held at Mannarkkad from November 18 to 21. More than 7,000 students are expected to take part in the fair.
General Education Minister N. Samsudheen unveiled the logo of the fair at a function held at Darunnajath Higher Secondary School, Nellipuzha, Mannarkkad, on Tuesday.

The Minister also chaired a review meeting to assess the preparations made by various committees and subcommittees. He asked the committees to ensure that all facilities, including accommodation and food, were arranged for the participating students and teachers. He also sought the cooperation of all sections to make the event a success.

The mathematics fair will be held at Kalladi Higher Secondary School, Kumaramputhur; the social science fair at MET Higher Secondary School, Mannarkkad; the work experience fair at Darunnajath Higher Secondary School, Nellipuzha; and the science and IT fairs at MES Higher Secondary School, Mannarkkad.

The Young Innovators Programme (YIP) Sasthrapadham idea exhibition will also be held at MES Higher Secondary School. The skill festival exhibition and career fest will be organised at Mini Mubas Stadium at Nellipuzha. The skill festival will be held at GMUP School, Mannarkkad.
The fair will be organised in compliance with green protocol. Temporary traffic regulations will be introduced to ensure smooth movement of vehicles. Cultural programmes will be held every evening.

K. Premkumar, MLA, presided over the function. Mannarkkad municipal chairperson K. Sajna, block panchayat president Neethu Shankar, Education department officials, programme committee representatives and headteachers of various schools attended.

articles.title: Domestic rooftop solar installations in T.N. remain low due to policy challenges, say consumers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With 425.61 MW of domestic rooftop solar installations in Tamil Nadu that have benefited from the PM Surya Ghar scheme, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation is taking efforts to bring more households under rooftop solar.
However, industry and consumer representatives say the State government should address a couple of basic policy issues so that more households go in for rooftop solar.

“While the government advertisements claim that consumers will get to pay nothing as bi-monthly energy charges if they instal rooftop solar, in reality, they have to pay network charges,” says K. Kathirmathiyon, secretary of Coimbatore Consumer Cause.

A.D. Thirumurthi, advisor of the National Solar Energy Federation of India, says the consumers should be exempted from network charges for rooftop solar. Further, in the case of additional solar energy generated in a financial year that goes unused, the consumers should be paid at least the average power purchase cost for the excess solar energy they feed to the grid.

Mr. Kathirmathiyon explained that if a consumer instals a five KW rooftop solar and his bi-monthly consumption is 500-550 units, he will supply the excess to the grid. He does not get any payment for the additional power. Instead, he will have to pay nearly ₹5,800 annually as network charges. Why should a consumer pay for solar energy that he has generated and not consumed, he asks.

“Tamil Nadu should adopt an approach similar to Kerala instead of allowing surplus electricity credits to lapse without compensation. Network charges applicable to domestic rooftop solar investors under the TNERC tariff framework with effect from October 22, 2021 constitute another major disincentive,” he says.

The Government and the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission should ensure domestic rooftop solar power producer/consumer is paid for the surplus electricity remaining unadjusted at the end of the settlement period (31st March). It should also withdraw network/wheeling charges levied on domestic rooftop solar power producers.
Mr. Thirumurthi says residents who consume more than 500 units of electricity in two months stand to benefit more if they go in for solar. The government should take steps to encourage them, he said.

However, industry and consumer representatives say the State government should address a couple of basic policy issues so that more households go in for rooftop solar.

“While the government advertisements claim that consumers will get to pay nothing as bi-monthly energy charges if they instal rooftop solar, in reality, they have to pay network charges,” says K. Kathirmathiyon, secretary of Coimbatore Consumer Cause.

A.D. Thirumurthi, advisor of the National Solar Energy Federation of India, says the consumers should be exempted from network charges for rooftop solar. Further, in the case of additional solar energy generated in a financial year that goes unused, the consumers should be paid at least the average power purchase cost for the excess solar energy they feed to the grid.

Mr. Kathirmathiyon explained that if a consumer instals a five KW rooftop solar and his bi-monthly consumption is 500-550 units, he will supply the excess to the grid. He does not get any payment for the additional power. Instead, he will have to pay nearly ₹5,800 annually as network charges. Why should a consumer pay for solar energy that he has generated and not consumed, he asks.

“Tamil Nadu should adopt an approach similar to Kerala instead of allowing surplus electricity credits to lapse without compensation. Network charges applicable to domestic rooftop solar investors under the TNERC tariff framework with effect from October 22, 2021 constitute another major disincentive,” he says.

The Government and the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission should ensure domestic rooftop solar power producer/consumer is paid for the surplus electricity remaining unadjusted at the end of the settlement period (31st March). It should also withdraw network/wheeling charges levied on domestic rooftop solar power producers.

Mr. Thirumurthi says residents who consume more than 500 units of electricity in two months stand to benefit more if they go in for solar. The government should take steps to encourage them, he said.

articles.title: India Post being modernised with focus on technology, customer service: Pemmasani
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union Minister inspects post offices and BSNL infrastructure in Bhopal; stresses faster postal services and improved connectivity

India Post is being comprehensively modernised through the adoption of advanced technology and a customer-centric approach to deliver faster and better-quality services, Union Minister of State for Communications Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar said.

According to a press release issued by the Minister’s camp office in Guntur, Dr. Chandra Sekhar made the remarks during surprise inspections of two major post offices in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, on Tuesday. He said the postal department was being strengthened to function with the efficiency and service standards of a corporate organisation while retaining public trust.

He inspected counter services, ticketing systems, parcel delivery networks, mail handling and other modern facilities. He also interacted with postal employees to understand their workplace challenges and requirements and sought feedback from customers and members of the public on service quality and the problems they faced.

He said India Post had evolved beyond letter delivery into a major public service network offering banking and insurance facilities. Efforts to strengthen its operations had been intensified over the past two-and-a-half years.
He highlighted the expansion of banking services through India Post Payments Bank and the digital transformation of Postal Life Insurance.
Later, he reviewed BSNL’s network and technical infrastructure in Bhopal and directed officials to ensure uninterrupted high-speed connectivity and improve telecommunications services.

articles.title: U.S. President Donald Trump nominates Natalie Baker as next Ambassador to Pakistan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome

U.S. President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker to be the next U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan , paving the way for the appointment of a permanent envoy to Islamabad after a gap of nearly two years, it emerged on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
Ms. Baker is currently serving as charge d’affaires at the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad. She assumed the role in January 2025, following the departure of then-ambassador Donald Armin Blome.

The White House, in a statement, said the nomination has been submitted to the U.S. Senate, whose foreign relations committee will review it. If approved by the committee, the nomination will proceed to a vote by the full Senate. Ms. Baker would be appointed as the U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan following the Senate’s confirmation.

Earlier, she had arrived in Islamabad as Deputy Chief of Mission in August 2024, according to details available on the embassy’s website. Prior to that, she served as the Deputy Chief of Mission at the U.S. Embassy in Doha from August 2021 to July 2024.

Ms. Baker was also deployed as the Deputy Chief of Mission and charge d’affaires of the U.S. Mission to Libya, deputy director of the Iran Regional Presence Office at the U.S. consulate in Dubai and economic counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Kuwait.

She also served as the director of the Office of North African Affairs in the U.S. State Department’s Near Eastern Affairs Bureau. Ms. Baker is quite active in Islamabad and frequently interacts with local officials and the political leadership of Pakistan. She also oversaw the marked improvement in ties between Pakistan and the U.S. during the tenure of President Trump.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) arrived in Denmark to discuss military support, air defence and energy infrastructure security with Nordic leaders, Danish authorities said.

"I am proud to welcome President Zelensky and the Nordic leaders to Denmark. The Ukrainians' fight for a free Ukraine and a free Europe continues," Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said in a statement.
The Nordic countries are among the main supporters of Ukraine and Zelensky travelled to Oslo at the end of October to meet with American envoys.
Direct negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow, under U.S. mediation, also began on Tuesday (November 10) in Abu Dhabi.
"Almost five years after the full-scale invasion, the rain of bombs targeting civilians, relief centres, and water and heating plants continues. That is why we must stand firm," Mr. Frederiksen said.

Copenhagen police announced Tuesday (November 10) that they would increase security in public spaces for the coming days. They have introduced a ban on the use of drones over the capital until November 12.

articles.title: Pannun’s civil lawsuit: U.S. court allows Pannun to serve NSA Doval and former intelligence chief Goyal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Order issued on November 9, 2026, after State department attempts to serve Indian officials via Embassy, MEA rejects charges as “frivolous”, calls Pannun’s case “fabricated and malicious”

A U.S. court on Monday (November 9, 2026) allowed Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun to serve his civil plea on National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former R&AW intelligence chief Samant Goel through Indian judicial channels, after the State Department submitted that it had served the notice for the two officials at the Indian Embassy in Washington.

The move was rejected by the Ministry of External Affairs, which said such judicial documents must go to the Ministry of Law and Justice in India and called Mr. Pannun’s civil lawsuit “frivolous”. The lawsuit filed by Mr. Pannun, who is wanted in India on terror charges, is separate but linked to the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)’s findings of an assassination plot against Mr. Pannun in June 2023. An undercover Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) informant had pointed to Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, and to conversations with senior Indian intelligence officials including Vikash Yadav for a conspiracy to hire a hitman to kill Mr. Pannun in New York. Mr. Gupta has subsequently pleaded guilty to all the charges, and the courts have set November 20 as the date for his sentencing. Mr. Yadav was arrested in Delhi in December 2023 on separate charges by Indian authorities and given bail in April 2024.

The FBI in the U.S. and Canadian officials investigating a similar case involving the killing of Harjeet Singh Nijjar in Vancouver in June 2023 appear to have dropped earlier claims of the involvement of more senior officials, including NSA Doval, former R&AW chief Samant Goyal, and Home Minister Amit Shah. However, Mr. Pannun has sought to pursue his case further and has filed several petitions demanding that Mr. Doval and Mr. Goyal be summoned by the court. In February 2025, when Mr. Doval accompanied Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Washington for a bilateral visit and meeting with US President Donald Trump, Mr. Pannun had tried to serve the NSA with a notice and failed.

The Ministry of External Affairs indicated on Tuesday (November 10) that it was unconcerned by the latest development in the case, and that the procedure for issuing the notice would require engaging the Law Ministry directly, not via the Embassy or the MEA.

“We reject the fabricated and malicious attacks on our high officials, as also we reject the frivolous lawsuits. Request for serving of judicial documents in India can only be routed through India’s designated central authority, that is the Ministry of Law and Justice,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to questions at a regular briefing.

Granting permission for the summons on Monday (November 9), U.S. District Judge Katherine Polk Failla directed Mr. Pannun to prepare a number of documents on or before November 30, including the summons addressed to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goyal, details of Indian law and procedure and the route by which the summons would be issued, as well as records of previous attempts at serving the two officials under the Hague Convention.

The certificate of submission delivered to the Indian Embassy by the State Department was signed by an official and dated October 9, 2026. Neither the Embassy nor the MEA had commented on the issue. The State Department said in a footnote that the delivery did not mean it was taking a “position” on the case and was a “legal obligation.

articles.title: Government plans curbs on film promotions and commercial events in educational institutions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The proposed guidelines are expected to restrict the use of educational institution premises for non-academic, political film promotions and unrelated commercial events

The government is considering a ban on film promotions and other commercial activities on the premises of educational institutions following a series of incidents involving unauthorised events and alleged safety lapses.

The government is examining the activities that educational institutions can legally conduct on their campuses and those that should be prohibited. Senior officials of the Education department have been asked to prepare guidelines to regulate such activities.

The proposed guidelines are expected to restrict the use of educational institution premises for non-academic, political film promotions and unrelated commercial events. The move comes amid allegations that some private educational institutions have been using students for political and other purposes.

In recent times, some colleges not only declared a holiday to facilitate film promotion events but also recommended students to watch those films. Such practices have also drawn criticism from educationists.

The concern has been compounded by incidents in which students have lost their lives during events organised on institutional premises. In a recent incident, a stage erected for an event at an educational institution collapsed, killing a student and injuring several others.

Under the proposed framework, institutions organising large-scale academic, sports or cultural events may be required to submit advance details to local Education department officials and the police. These would include the expected number of participants, arrangements for stage construction, entry and exit points, crowd management and fire safety measures.

The government is understood to be considering a distinction between minor events intended to encourage students’ sporting, artistic and cultural talents and large gatherings that interfere with academic activities.

Officials point out that the government is keen on activities to promote arts, culture and creativity among students and has over the past three years launched several initiatives to promote skills, employment, innovation and entrepreneurship among them.. However, decision of certain educational institutions to promote particular films and even declare holidays to enable students to watch them has invited criticism from parents and educationists.

articles.title: Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College, dies at 81
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre, popularly known as Barefoot College, in Tilonia in 1972

One of the foundational figures of modern civil society in India and the founder of Barefoot College, Sanjit “Bunker” Roy, died at his home in Tilonia, in Rajasthan’s Ajmer district, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) morning. He was 81.

“He went peacefully as he wanted to in his own home in Tilonia, surrounded by Aruna and some of the countless people who loved and cared for him deeply, passionately,” said a statement issued by the Social Work and Research Centre (SWRC) – Barefoot College.

He was 21 years old when famine struck Bihar in 1966. Consecutive monsoons had failed. Seeing the horrors of extreme poverty, with people dropping dead of starvation, changed the course of his life, and he decided to spurn the “whole world laid out for him”.

Bunker Roy's activism began at a time when social work was often viewed with disdain. His wife and prominent activist, Aruna Roy, recalls in her memoir, The Personal is Political, that when she was serving as a sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) in Delhi, a chief metropolitan magistrate reacted dismissively after learning that Bunker Roy was a social worker. “ Kahin naukri nahin mili hogi (He must not have landed a job anywhere),” her colleague quipped. The magistrate’s attitude changed dramatically, however, when he later discovered that Bunker Roy was the national squash champion, and promptly sought Roy's help in securing membership to the prestigious Delhi Gymkhana Club.

Roy studied at the Doon School alongside future Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and attended St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, between 1962 and 1967. He won the national squash championship in 1965 and represented India in three world championships. In a TED Talk posted online 15 years ago, he described his elite education as “snobbish” and “expensive”, saying it had “almost destroyed” him.

In 1972, Roy founded the Social Work and Research Centre in Tilonia, Rajasthan, which later became widely known as Barefoot College. In the same TED Talk, he described it as “a place for cop-outs, drop-outs and wash-outs” and not for certificate chasers. It had a bottom-up approach, enabling the villagers to “identify their own challenges, develop local solutions and manage their resources independently”, working towards community-based water management and renewable energy initiatives.

Paying tribute, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said Roy’s vision of training rural grandmothers as “Barefoot Solar Engineers” had helped bring electricity to thousands of off-grid homes across India and other developing countries, while advancing community empowerment and environmental stewardship.

Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh recalled Roy as a jovial figure whose love of chocolates earned opprobrium from Mr. Ramesh’s wife for polishing off an entire box without sharing. Mr. Ramesh said Roy believed that civil society “must cooperate where they can, collaborate where they should, and confront where they must". Roy, he said, worked closely with the Rajiv Gandhi government in areas such as drinking water, immunisation, and adult literacy.
Sam Pitroda, who served as an adviser to Rajiv Gandhi and worked with Roy, remembered him as an “institution-builder” whose impact extended far beyond the communities he served.
Former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot said Roy made significant contributions to rural self-reliance, education, and development while drawing inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi’s principles.
CPI general secretary D. Raja described Roy as a pioneering social activist and educationist whose work would continue to inspire those committed to equality, dignity, and social justice.

Writer Amitav Ghosh noted that despite opportunities to pursue a distinguished career in diplomacy, the bureaucracy, or the corporate world, Roy chose instead to dedicate his life to addressing rural poverty, calling him “a true hero”.

articles.title: Juvenile traced to Srinagar for sending fake Delhi Police notices targeting IFF, SFLC X accounts; Crime Branch registers FIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: X had told the Delhi High Court that the takedown requests purportedly issued in the name of the Delhi Police were fraudulent; the force’s IFSO unit will assist in the investigation

The Delhi Police’s Crime Branch has registered a case over fraudulent notices purportedly issued in the name of the force, seeking the removal of social media posts and the blocking of accounts belonging to the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and the Software Freedom Law Centre (SFLC), an official close to the development told The Hindu.
A juvenile has been traced to Srinagar in connection with the impersonation, sources said.
The FIR has been registered on charges of impersonating a public servant and forgery under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Section 66 of Information Technology (IT) Act.

The development comes days after social media platform X told the Delhi High Court that an internal investigation had established that the notices were not genuine police communications and had been sent by an “imposter”. The platform also told the court that it had not acted on the requests and would not take down the organisations’ accounts.

The case follows a November 6 hearing before Justice Amit Mahajan, who was hearing petitions filed by the two digital rights organisations challenging the purported takedown requests. X’s counsel told the court that the platform had conducted an internal investigation and found that someone had impersonated the Delhi Police.
“We did not act on it. Notices are not sent by the Delhi Police. We have filed a complaint with the Delhi Police last night to find the imposter,” X’s counsel submitted.
The court recorded the platform’s assurance and disposed of the petitions, granting the organisations liberty to approach it again if any action was taken against their accounts.

The controversy began after X forwarded two purported ‘Illegal Content Reports’ to IFF on November 3. The first, dated October 31, sought the removal of a post published by IFF on October 30 and another post by SFLC. The second, dated November 2, sought the removal of 37 posts and the blocking of three accounts — @internetfreedom, @SFLCin and @geoblockedindia — in their entirety.

The notices alleged that the posts were “defamatory” towards the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). They reportedly called for the content to be removed or withheld within three hours, citing provisions of the Information Technology Act and the IT Rules, 2021.

IFF had said that the posts in question reproduced and commented on a legal notice purportedly sent to the organisation on behalf of the RSS. It maintained that the posts constituted protected speech under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution and that it had not been given prior notice before the takedown requests were submitted.
The organisation subsequently served a legal notice on the Delhi Police and X Corp. through its counsel, seeking clarification over the requests.

SFLC, meanwhile, had questioned the authenticity of the communications after attempting to verify them with the Delhi Police. It said an email sent to the address mentioned in the purported notices was returned as undelivered, with an error stating that the user did not exist. The organisation pointed out that the same email address was listed on the Delhi Police website at the time, further raising questions about the communications.

articles.title: Akhilesh to visit Ram Temple; promises to transform Ayodhya into capital of Sanatan pilgrimage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Uttar Pradesh BJP challenged Mr. Yadav to visit the Temple on December 6 — anniversary of the Babri Masjid demolition — and apologise for the killing of kar sevaks

A war of words has erupted over the Samajwadi Party (SP) president and former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav’s plan to visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on December 12. This would be his first visit since its consecration in January 2024.

Making a statement on Tuesday, the Uttar Pradesh BJP president, Pankaj Chaudhary, challenged Mr. Yadav to visit the Temple on December 6 — anniversary of the Babri Masjid demolition — and apologise for the killing of kar sevaks during SP rule.

“If this is true repentance and not a new trick on Lord Shri Ram, visit the Temple on 6th December, not 12th. Hundreds of devotees were murdered. Apologize for that sin. Do not think that your past sins will be washed away,” wrote Mr. Chaudhary, on X.

Amid the uproar Mr. Yadav promised to make Ayodhya the global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage. “We are committed to restoring the honor and dignity of Ayodhya. We will improve and enhance it so the number of visitors to Ayodhya is boosted. Their numbers have been dwindling due to the theft at the Temple, which has directly impacted the local economy. We will also strive to restore trust by providing a transparent system. By building world-class infrastructure, we will make Ayodhya the ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’,” Mr. Yadav wrote on X.

The SP president went on to add, “We will build an Ayodhya where no arrogant person insults or harasses a poor woman or child collecting a little oil, and beats them with a cane. We will regain power and fulfill the nutritional needs of our citizens by providing oil and ghee. We will promote traditional boating so the boatmen can benefit and the strong bond between Lord Ram and the Nishadraj can be re-established. The BJP is trying to break this connection; it seeks to use its hegemony to ensure no one remembers the close ties Lord Ram and the PDA community shared.”

“We will free Ayodhya from outside contractors and initiate a land investigation. Outsiders have looted Ayodhya. None of the BJP leaders and corrupt officials involved in the circle rate scam will be spared. Their coffers, filled with the loot from Ayodhya, will be emptied. We will establish a system to ensure no evil-minded person can insult — or walk free after insulting — not just Lord Ram or Lord Krishna but also the deities and great men of other faiths. Such individuals will be legally detained. Those who harbour such unrighteous individuals who use abusive language are also partners in sin; they too will be punished for their involvement in the conspiracy to disrupt social harmony,” added the SP chief.

articles.title: New Israeli parliament to take aim at Netanyahu as Eisenkot seeks government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israel's new parliament convened on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) with plans to take aim immediately at caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as his rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to quickly cobble together a new government.

Mr. Eisenkot, leading a broad left-to-right bloc, will control the agenda from the outset in the new parliament with the help of Israeli-Arab parties, although neither he nor the right-wing Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, hold a majority on their own.

"I am committed in this complex situation to form a national-emergency government as quickly as possible," Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief who only recently entered politics, said before his swearing-in.
President Isaac Herzog, ceremonially opening the session, called on all sides to work together and avoid a fresh election in a deeply polarised country weary from three years of war.
"Nearly 80% of the people went to the polls and elected you. You must do everything to avoid a repeat election," Mr. Herzog said.
"Reach out a hand for compromise, even between rivals."

Mr. Eisenkot's allies hope to use their newfound legislative power to move rapidly on key priorities, including a commission to investigate security failures under Netanyahu that allowed the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, the deadliest day in Israel's history.
ALSO WATCH Israel’s Eisenkot invites Netanyahu to join government under his leadership

Mr. Herzog on Sunday (November 8, 2026) gave Mr. Eisenkot the initial mandate to form a government, starting the clock for him to piece together a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

Hours before the opening of the Parliament, known as the Knesset, Mr. Eisenkot's party announced agreements on key people to replace allies of Mr. Netanyahu, who has been in and out of office for nearly 20 years.
Mr. Eisenkot's bloc announced it had the votes to install as parliament speaker Matan Kahana, a former senior military figure who clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews during a past stint in government.
Avigdor Liberman, a right-wing member of Eisenkot's bloc who has played a key role in deciding who can enter the government, will be nominated as chair of the foreign affairs and defence committee.

articles.title: EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra warns 'expectations low' from COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: "If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," Wopke Hoekstra said

The European Union ’s (EU) top climate official admitted on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) that expectations were "low" from the COP31 summit in Turkiye, while holding out hope for "meaningful" progress on the topic of clean electricity.

"Expectations are low — that's just a reflection of reality," European Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told a group of reporters including from AFP , arguing that electrification should be the core focus of the United Nations climate talks .
"If indeed we manage to make electrification the sole focus, or close to the sole focus of the COP, I think we have a chance to deliver on something that is truly meaningful," he said.

The European commissioner will travel to the Turkish resort of Antalya on Monday (November 9, 2026) for the talks which run until November 20. Mr. Hoekstra voiced hope that setting an electrification target would be "at the heart" of the summit conclusions, adding: "Of course, the cleaner that electrification is, the better it is."
ALSO WATCH COP31: Can negotiators finally deliver results? | The Hindu explains

Host nation Turkiye is inviting countries to join a voluntary "electrification" pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20% today to 35% by 2035. But the EU's call for "clean" electrification could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.
Observers expect few major breakthroughs from COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the U.S. war with Iran and Russia's conflict in Ukraine.
The talks are also missing a major player since U.S. President Donald Trump who pulled Washington out of the Paris climate agreement has not sent officials to the talks.

"The larger picture is that the geopolitics of the times we live in are extremely complicated," said Mr. Hoekstra, who acknowledged that a string of recent COP meetings had been "underwhelming in terms of their delivery".
"There are substantial questions to be asked on how fit for purpose this design actually still is, with its unanimity" system that does not always deliver "what is actually needed," he said.

The EU has previously warned there would be no political will for extra funding pledges at COP31, a message Mr. Hoekstra repeated. "Europe is at the absolute top of delivering on climate finance, not just for ourselves but also for others," Mr. Hoekstra said, calling for a push for "more burden sharing".

Environmental groups have criticised a series of recent European rollbacks on climate, most lately plans to postpone rules targeting methane, a highly potent greenhouse gas. But Mr. Hoekstra pushed back at the notion the EU was backsliding on its ambitions.

articles.title: Iran rejects France’s ‘baseless accusations’ on cyberattack
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food
Iran on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were “baseless”.
“Iran’s Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France,” the Ministry said in a statement.
It added that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.
Similar incidents were then reported in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

Along with summoning Iran’s ambassador and seeking European-level sanctions, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Tuesday that Paris would “rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks”.
Tehran meanwhile said it would “not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities”.
It added that France “is merely projecting its own governance failures” with these accusations.
“A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations,” it continued.
Also on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the European Union said it would look to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states after France’s announcement.

🌐 International Affairs 📅 10 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Iran rejects France’s ‘baseless accusations’ on cyberattack

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food

Iran on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were “baseless”.

“Iran’s Foreign Ministry categorically rejects the French government’s baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France,” the Ministry said in a statement.

It added that it “strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic”.

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

Similar incidents were then reported in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

Along with summoning Iran’s ambassador and seeking European-level sanctions, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Tuesday that Paris would “rule nothing out and will take all measures — including those we may not disclose publicly — that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks”.

Tehran meanwhile said it would “not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities”.

It added that France “is merely projecting its own governance failures” with these accusations.

“A government that cannot even manage the temperature of its own refrigerators now seeks to shift the blame onto foreign actors through these preposterous accusations,” it continued.

Also on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), the European Union said it would look to provide a “swift and united response” pending discussion with member states after France’s announcement.

articles.title: Without any rationale: on the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Caste and class: on OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992), the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026), the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: NMDC said to be in talks with Russia’s Rosatom over lithium investments
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel, however, are developing the country’s largest lithium deposit through their PolarLithium joint venture, with commercial production expected to begin by 2030

Indian state-run miner NMDC Ltd. is in talks with Russia’s Rosatom to invest in Russian lithium projects, three people familiar with the matter said, as India steps up efforts to secure supplies of the metal for its battery and EV industries.
NMDC officials visited Russia last month for a conference and also held talks with state nuclear firm Rosatom, two of the people said.

The third person, who also confirmed that company officials had met with Rosatom, said NMDC was keen to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities in Russia and had also held discussions with other Russian companies.

All three people, who asked not to be named as the talks were confidential, said discussions between NMDC and Rosatom remain preliminary. A Rosatom spokesperson did not address Reuters queries about the meetings last month but said the Russian company was not currently engaged in talks with NMDC.

fullParagraphs: The announcement followed the 23rd meeting ​of the ‌GCC’s Joint Defence Council, attended by Defence Ministers from the bloc’s member states, in Bahrain

The six Gulf Cooperation Council states have ​approved the establishment of an ‌advanced headquarters for their Unified Military ​Command in Kuwait ⁠and the deployment of “appropriate” forces to it, the bloc’s secretary-general said.

The GCC established ‌its Unified Military Command ​at a summit in Kuwait in December 2013 to plan ⁠and manage joint military operations and strengthen member states’ defence capabilities against ‌potential threats to their territory, airspace, waters and interests.

The ⁠war has disrupted air travel and ⁠shipping, and raised concerns over the security of the ‌region’s vital oil and gas exports.

articles.title: Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Myanmar's military has seized a key resistance military command headquarters and 10 other bases in the south of the country, state media reported on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), marking a new gain by the army in the civil war as it seeks control of regions long held by resistance forces.
The capture of the bases in the jungle along the border between Mon state and the Bago region marks the latest setback suffered by pro-democracy armed groups and ethnic militias fighting the army.
The reported capture could not be independently confirmed because the military does not allow journalists free access to the area, but the claim has not been challenged.

The military-backed government, which took office in April following controversial elections earlier this year, has stepped up activity in recent months on the ground and with airstrikes to retake areas controlled by the People's Defense Force, the armed wing of the major opposition National Unity Government, and ethnic militias that have been fighting the central government for greater autonomy for decades.
The PDF emerged after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in February 2021 and has since formed loose alliances with ethnic militias fighting the military.

A report in the state-run Myanma Alinn newspaper on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) said the army captured 11 bases operating in the jungle area straddling the border between Mon and Bago during a six-day operation that began a week ago.

The captured positions included the special region command headquarters of the NUG and a battalion headquarters of the Karen National Liberation Army, the armed wing of the Karen National Union, a major Karen ethnic rebel group.
The paper published photos showing soldiers who captured the bases alongside ammunition seized during the operation.
Small arms, ammunition supplies, vehicles, drones and computers were captured after four armed engagements, the report said, adding that the military would continue security operations in the region.
The NUG and KNU did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The captured regions, about 120 kilometers (75 miles) northeast of Yangon, the country's largest city, have seen intense conflict since the 2021 military takeover that prompted widespread public protests. The violent suppression of the demonstrations by government security forces triggered an armed resistance that has led to civil war.

The NUG's special region command headquarters said in a previous social media statement that it had 12 PDF battalions, seven drones with specialized support units, as well as six combat and defence units under its command. It also said it was conducting military operations across the southern Kayin and Mon states, as well as the Bago region. Kayin state is also known as Karen state.

articles.title: Israeli forces shoot dead 14-year-old in West Bank: Palestinian officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Israeli forces shot dead a 14-year-old in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials said, with Israel saying it was responding to stone-throwing.
Moutaz Eyad Daghlas was killed in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, late on Monday (November 9, 2026), the Palestinian health ministry said.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds and took them to hospital, but that Israeli forces blocked access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.
The Israeli military, asked by AFP about the incident, said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) it had acted to "thwart stone-hurling and terrorist attacks" in the area.

"The soldiers identified several terrorists who intended to hurl stones at a highway used by Israeli vehicles. This was in an area where stones have recently been hurled at Israeli vehicles," the military said.
"The soldiers responded by firing towards them in order to remove the threat."
Israeli forces have routinely opened live fire on Palestinians including minors who throw stones in the West Bank, which Israel has controlled since 1967.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem said Israeli forces killed at least 241 children or teenagers in the territory between the October 7, 2023 attack by Gaza-based Hamas and late June this year.

Violence has increased in recent weeks, especially in the run-up to Israel's October 27 election, before which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had sought to appeal to hardline settlers in the West Bank.
On October 23, Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint near Hebron before being killed by Israeli forces, who later responded with a major operation in the flashpoint city.

Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,116 Palestinians, both civilians and militants, in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, according to an AFP tally based on Palestinian Authority figures.
Palestinian attacks or clashes between Palestinians and Israeli forces have killed at least 51 Israelis during the same period, according to official Israeli figures.

articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

A few kilometres from the entrance to Arunachal Pradesh’s Parong village, an unpaved road winds all the way down to the Siang river. At dusk, all that is visible at the beginning of the dirt road is the glint of freshly painted yellow barricades of the State police and the shine from the silver of the concertina wires that connect the barricades. The Central security forces who guard the check post here have two purposes — to respond to “unrest” and to stop anyone without “clearance” from proceeding to Siang’s waters.

Parong, in Siang district, is one of the three proposed sites identified by the State government for a Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) to begin work on the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).

The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told.
